```
## 6. Best Buddy Ladder

### Heart thresholds (lifetime hearts earned with that Pokémon as buddy)
| Level | Hearts | Badge |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Buddy | 0 | (none) |
| **Good Buddy** | 1 | Good Buddy badge |
| **Great Buddy** | 70 | Great Buddy |
| **Ultra Buddy** | 150 | Ultra Buddy |
| **Best Buddy** | 300 | Best Buddy + ribbon |

([gamerant – Best Buddy CP boost](https://gamerant.com/pokemon-go-best-buddy-cp-boost/))

### Hearts per day
- **Normal mood**: up to **10 hearts/day** (12 with Poffin)
- **Excited mood**: up to **20 hearts/day**
- Earned via: feed, walk (per 1/2/3/4 km depending on species), play, snapshot, battle together, visit new stop, etc.

### Best Buddy CP boost — the key mechanic
- **+1 level equivalent** to **CPM only while that Pokémon is the active buddy**.
- Mathematically: while active, the CP is recomputed using the CPM of **one level higher**. A L50 Best Buddy uses **CPM 0.8453** (the L51 anchor) instead of L50's 0.8403.
- Switch buddies → the boost is removed (the Pokémon retains the Best Buddy *badge/ribbon* but not the CP).
- This boost **never lets you exceed the max stat** for league caps in the sense that the Pokémon's "true" level remains its raw level; PvP IV rankings use the raw level. For Master League and raids the boost is **live damage**.

### 2025-2026 buddy changes
- Routes integration (Sponsored Routes) increased hearts-per-route slightly in 2024; no material formula change in 2025.
- Daily Adventure Incense interactions count toward buddy hearts in some modes.
- L70+ trainers have an increased Lucky Friend chance during the daily buddy interaction.
- No evidence of a buddy-CP-boost magnitude change in 2025-2026.

---

## 7. Lucky Pokémon

- **Triggered by:** trading. Each trade has a chance to produce a "Lucky" outcome; chance scales with the **age** of the **older** of the two Pokémon being traded (older = higher chance). One stale Pokémon + one fresh Pokémon is identical to two stale.
- **Distance bonus:** trading two Pokémon caught **≥ 100 km apart** boosts lucky odds to **5%**.
- **Lucky Friend status** (separate): once you are Best Friends (90-day milestone), each first interaction of the day has a small chance to flag both parties as Lucky Friends. The **next trade with that friend is a guaranteed Lucky Trade**.
- **Lucky Pokémon properties:**
  - **IV floor 12/12/12** (so min 14% chance of hundo per stat; the per-Pokémon hundo rate is **1/64**)
  - Stardust power-up cost **halved (0.5×)**
  - Visually marked with a gold sparkly background.
- L70+ trainers see an **increased chance of becoming Lucky Friends** (a benefit of the new L80 system).

Sources: ([Wondershare / drfone – trading discount guide](https://drfone.wondershare.com/virtual-location/stardust-trade-cost-pokemon-go.html)), ([dittobase – hundo odds](https://www.dittobase.com/pokemon-go/hundo-odds)).

---

## 8. Shadow & Purified Pokémon

### Shadow (Team GO Rocket / Shadow Raid)
- Possess the **Frustration** charged move (a 2-bar Normal-type 10-power move). **Frustration can only be replaced during specific TGR takeover events** with a regular Charged TM; otherwise it occupies one slot permanently.
- **Damage multipliers** (apply only to shadow attacker):
  - Attack stat × **1.2** (effectively +20% damage they deal)
  - Defense stat × **0.833** (≈ –17%, takes more damage)
- **Power-up cost multipliers** (vs. non-shadow):
  - Stardust cost × **1.2**
  - Candy cost × **1.2**
  - Second-charged-move unlock × 1.2 (Stardust + Candy)
- **IV floors:**
  - TGR grunt/leader catch: **0/0/0** (weather-boosted: 4/4/4)
  - Shadow Raid: **6/6/6** (7/7/7 boosted)
  - Giovanni shadow legendary: **6/6/6**

### Purification
- Removes Shadow status. Replaces Frustration with **Return** (a 130-power Normal charged move, 2 bars).
- **Each IV increased by 2** (cap 15). So a 13/13/13 shadow → 15/15/15 hundo after purification.
- Pokémon **gains +1 level** (Pokémon below L25 are bumped to L25 — verify against current game master).
- Power-up / second-move / evolve costs become **lower than even a normal Pokémon** (the discount is a deliberate purification incentive).
- Stardust+Candy cost to purify is per-species — example: **Weedle 1 000 dust + 1 candy → Legendary up to 20 000 dust + 20 candy**.
- ([pokemongo.fandom – purification cost](https://pokemongo.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_purification_cost))

### Practical note
A Shadow Pokémon with **Frustration unlocked** (i.e., Frustration TM'd out during a TGR event) plus a high-DPS legacy charged move is the most damage-efficient PvE attacker class in the game.

---

## 9. Adventure Effect Mechanic

### How it works
- Activated via the **Charged Move detail screen** on a qualifying Pokémon (i.e., the Pokémon must currently *know* the right signature charged move). The button "Activate Adventure Effect" appears.
- **Costs Stardust + that species' Candy** per activation.
- **Duration** is fixed per effect: **6 minutes or 10 minutes** depending on the move.
- **Extension:** all current Adventure Effects can be **extended** by paying more Stardust+Candy, up to a **24-hour daily cap of total active time per effect** ([dittobase guide](https://www.dittobase.com/pokemon-go/guides/how-to-use-pokemon-go-adventure-effects)).
- **Concurrency:** only **one** Adventure Effect can be active at a time. Activating a second cancels/replaces the first.
- **No explicit cooldown** between activations beyond the 24-hour-per-day cap.
- The "charges-remaining today" / "next-available-at" indicator is encoded in the Pokémon's proto — likely fields on the per-Pokémon record (the game stores per-day usage rather than a global per-account quota). **Project TODO:** the project's note that this is encoded in `pokemon_size_category` is almost certainly wrong; the correct field is more likely `bonus_attack_uses_remaining` / `adventure_effect_remaining_uses` or a usage timestamp.

### Full Adventure Effect list as of 2026-05-27 (**9 effects, 9 Pokémon forms**)

| # | Pokémon (form)              | Move             | Effect                                                                                | Duration | Cost                              |
|---|-----------------------------|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|-----------------------------------|
| 1 | **Dialga (Origin Forme)**   | Roar of Time     | Pauses the timer on Incense, Daily Adventure Incense, Lucky Eggs, Star Pieces         | 6 min    | 5 000 dust + 5 Dialga candy       |
| 2 | **Palkia (Origin Forme)**   | Spacial Rend     | Increases the spawn radius for wild Pokémon around you                                | 10 min   | 5 000 dust + 5 Palkia candy       |
| 3 | **Necrozma (Dusk Mane)**    | Sunsteel Strike  | Game acts like it is daytime (day-only spawns appear; day-only evolutions work)       | 10 min   | 3 000 dust + 3 Necrozma candy     |
| 4 | **Necrozma (Dawn Wings)**   | Moongeist Beam   | Game acts like it is nighttime (night-only spawns appear; night-only evolutions work) | 10 min   | 3 000 dust + 3 Necrozma candy     |
| 5 | **Kyurem (Black)**          | Freeze Shock     | Wild encounters immobilized — easier to catch (+25%/+50% catch rate per source)       | 10 min   | 5 000 dust + 5 Kyurem candy       |
| 6 | **Kyurem (White)**          | Ice Burn         | Target ring slowed — easier Excellent throws (+50% catch rate)                        | 10 min   | 5 000 dust + 5 Kyurem candy       |

### Pokémon often **incorrectly assumed** to have Adventure Effects (do NOT)
Several legendaries are widely speculated about but **have not been confirmed as Adventure-Effect-bearing as of 2026-05-27**:
- **Calyrex (Ice Rider)** — Glacial Lance is a signature charged move but **no Adventure Effect** is associated as of this snapshot.
- **Calyrex (Shadow Rider)** — Astral Barrage is a signature charged move; **no Adventure Effect**.
- **Solgaleo / Lunala** standalone — only their **Necrozma fusion** forms have Adventure Effects.
- **Reshiram / Zekrom** standalone — only their **Kyurem fusion** forms have Adventure Effects.
- **Marshadow** — no Adventure Effect.

**For the project's `ADVENTURE_EFFECT_IDS` set:** the 9 species/forms above are the canonical set. If the project set lists fewer than 9, it's missing entries; if it lists more, those extras should be re-verified.

## 10. Mega Evolution

### Levels and progression (Mega Levels are **per individual Pokémon**, not per species)
| Mega Level | Mega Evolutions needed (cumulative) | Mega-Energy cost (per evo) | Cooldown to next Mega Evo |
|------------|-------------------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|
| **(0 — never)** | 0 | **200** | 14 days |
| **Level 1 — Base**           | 1                                       | **41**                         | 7 days  |
| **Level 2 — High**           | 7 (i.e. 6 more after Base)              | **21**                         | 5 days  |
| **Level 3 — Max**            | 30 (i.e. 23 more after High)            | **11**                         | 3 days  |
| **Super Max (eligible species)** | spend +5 000 Mega Energy after Max | (effectively free first time after Super Max) | 24 hours |

(Some sources call Level 3 "Max" and Level 4 "Super High" / "Super Max" depending on translation. The progression structure above is the consistently reported one.)

### Cooldown decrease
- A Pokémon at low Mega Level has a **7-day cooldown** (after first activation; 14 days for the very first ever).
- At **Max / Super Max**, the cooldown drops to **24 hours**.

### Bonuses by Mega Level
At every level, a Mega Evolved Pokémon while active gives the team:
- **+10% damage** to all attacks for other team members in raids/Max Battles
- **+30% damage** to attacks **matching the Mega's type(s)** (so a Mega Steelix gives Steel and Ground attacks +30%, everything else +10%)
- These boosts apply to *other* trainers' Pokémon, not the Mega holder's own non-Mega Pokémon in the same raid lobby

Mega Levels add:
- **Level 2 (High)**: +50 XP per catch while active, ~10% XL Candy chance per catch
- **Level 3 (Max)**: +100 XP per catch, +2 type-candy per catch, 25% XL Candy chance per catch

### Mega form duration
- **8 hours** by default. Some events extend this.
- After 8 hours expires, the Pokémon reverts; it then enters a cooldown (length depends on the Mega Level above).
- During the active 8 hours the Pokémon **cannot** be deployed in gyms or PvP (some restrictions apply).
- Catch candy bonuses: catching a Pokémon while a Mega of the same type is active gives +1 type Candy and a small XL Candy chance.

([dotesports – Mega Evolution levels and costs](https://dotesports.com/pokemon/news/pokemon-go-mega-evolution-levels-bonuses-cooldown-and-costs-explained) via search)

### 2025-2026 changes
- No structural Mega change in 2025; new Mega species were added (e.g., Mega Metagross debut at October 2025 Raid Day per gamerant). Energy thresholds and cooldowns are unchanged.

## 11. Trade Mechanics

### Friendship levels & duration to reach
| Friendship | Days of daily interaction |
|-----------|---------------------------|
| Friend (none / 0 hearts)     | 0 (just added)   |
| Good Friend                  | 1 day            |
| Great Friend                 | 7 days           |
| Ultra Friend                 | 30 days          |
| Best Friend                  | 90 days          |

### Trade stardust costs (Special vs Standard)

A trade is a **Special Trade** if **either** Pokémon is:
- Legendary or Mythical, OR
- Shiny, OR
- Different forms of a species (e.g., Spinda variants beyond what you've registered), OR
- A species the receiver has **not yet registered in Pokédex**.

You can do **1 Special Trade per day**, period (no friendship-level increases this).

**Stardust cost matrix (Special Trade):**

| Friendship | Legendary/Shiny | Unregistered (regional, etc.) |
|-----------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| Good      | 1 000 000 dust  | 20 000 dust                  |
| Great     | 800 000 dust    | 16 000 dust                  |
| Ultra     | 80 000 dust     | 1 600 dust                   |
| Best      | 40 000 dust     | 800 dust                     |

Standard (non-Special) trade costs scale similarly but cap at **100 dust** for Best Friend. (Friendship discounts: Great = ~20%, Ultra = 92%, Best = 96%.)

### Lucky trade odds
- Two new Pokémon: ~5% baseline Lucky chance (varies by source).
- **Guaranteed Lucky** (current rule, re-verified 2026-09-20): a trade where either Pokémon was caught in **2020 or earlier** is guaranteed Lucky until the trainer's lifetime allowance of **45** guaranteed Luckies is spent. The window and the allowance have moved: 25→35 on 2025-02-18 (window: caught 2019 or earlier), then 35→45 on 2025-12-31 (window: caught 2020 or earlier), the rule in force in 2026.
- Distance-bonus (≥100 km apart): **+5%** absolute Lucky chance.
- **Lucky Friend status** (from Best Friend interactions): **next trade with that friend is guaranteed Lucky.**

### Other trade attributes
- **Original Trainer (OT)** field is permanently stored on the Pokémon; OT-matching is a requirement for the Aura ribbon and Showcase eligibility-like fields. Trades pass OT to the new owner record.
- A traded Pokémon **cannot be re-traded**.
- IVs are **re-rolled** at trade time with the floor depending on friendship (see §2 table).

([imobie – special trade guide](https://www.imobie.com/pokemon-go/special-trade-pokemon-go.htm)), ([drfone – trade discount guide](https://drfone.wondershare.com/virtual-location/stardust-trade-cost-pokemon-go.html))

## 12. Bag / Inventory / Tag Limits

### Pokémon storage
- **Maximum Pokémon storage: 11 150** (as of **November 11, 2025** capacity increase, +650). ([Pokémon GO X/Twitter announcement](https://x.com/PokemonGoApp/status/1987988717370261973))
- Upgrades are purchased in 50-Pokémon increments from the in-game Shop.

### Item bag
- **Maximum item bag: 10 500** (as of Nov 11 2025, +1 000). Upgrades in 50-item increments.
- Default at L1 is 350 items; upgrade purchasable starting around L10.

### Tag system
- **Maximum distinct tags per account: 100**.
- **Tag colors:** 8 — Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Purple, Grey, Black.
- **Tag name length:** up to **16 characters**.
- **Tags per individual Pokémon:** **No publicly documented hard cap.** Niantic Help Center, Bulbapedia, Fandom Wiki, and Gamepur all describe tags as "multiple per Pokémon" but **none confirm a 14-tag-per-Pokémon limit**. The visual display only shows up to **3 tags** and an ellipsis (`…`). The "14" figure used by the project is **not corroborated by any reachable web source** — it is plausibly a project heuristic or an inference from the protobuf field size.
- **Trainer level requirement to use tags:** **L14+**.
- ([pokemongo.fandom – Tag](https://pokemongo.fandom.com/wiki/Tag)), ([gamepur – tag limits](https://www.gamepur.com/guides/all-tagging-colors-and-maximum-number-of-tags-you-can-have-in-pokemon-go))

**Action for the project:** verify the 14-tag-per-Pokemon assumption by either (a) inspecting an actual `Pokemon` proto extraction to count `pokemon_tag` repeated-field entries the game writes, or (b) experimentally tagging one Pokémon with >14 tags to see if the UI blocks the 15th. **Until verified, treat "14" as unconfirmed.**

## Summary of confirmed 2025-2026 changes

| Change | When | Source |
|--------|------|--------|

---

## Confidence / unresolved items

1. **CPM table**: resolved 2026-09-21 — read from the client game master (`PLAYER_LEVEL_SETTINGS` → `playerLevel.cpMultiplier`, 80 levels); see §1.
2. **`pokemon_size_category` integer enum 1–5 mapping**: assumed XXS=1..XXL=5 but **not** verified against the proto. Could be 0-indexed. Verify in extracted GAME_MASTER.
3. **14-tag-per-Pokémon limit**: **unconfirmed by any web source**. Display limit is 3 tags + "…"; the *applied* limit may be higher. Recommend in-game test or proto inspection.
4. **Mighty Pokémon IV floor**: resolved — **13/13/13** (verified 2026-09).
5. **Calyrex / Solgaleo / Lunala / Reshiram / Zekrom / Marshadow Adventure Effects**: standalone forms **do not** have Adventure Effects as of this snapshot. Only the **fusion forms** (Necrozma DM/DW, Kyurem B/W) carry them.
6. **Exact Adventure Effect daily-cap encoding in the proto**: the *charges-remaining* / next-eligible-time fields are encoded in the per-Pokémon proto but I could not confirm the exact field name from public sources. The project's prior speculation that uses-left lives in `pokemon_size_category` is almost certainly wrong — that column holds the size enum.
```

```md
**Season-long bonuses** (Memories in Motion):
- Lv 31+ get **1 guaranteed Candy XL** on in-person trade; +1 additional Candy on in-person trade
- Increased XP for 7-day PokéStop spin streak
- Increased XP **and** Stardust for 7-day catch streak

**Daily Discoveries** (the big season-exclusive feature — *Spotlight Hour is paused this season*):
- **Sunday** — Double-Time Sunday: Incense and Lure Modules last up to 2×
- **Monday** — Fast-Track Monday + Max Monday (rotating Dynamax bosses)
- **Tuesday** — **Showcase Tuesday** (PokéStop Showcases, ~20 categories, 10 a.m.–8 p.m.) — *this replaces the traditional Tuesday Spotlight Hour*
- **Wednesday** — 5-star Raid Boss rotation + Raid Hour 6–7 p.m.
- **Thursday** — Up to 4× Stardust GBL wins; daily set limit raised 5→10 (50 battles/day)
- **Friday** — Friendship Friday: up to 2 Special Trades, increased Lucky chance, reduced Stardust trade cost

There are **NO weekly Tuesday Spotlight Hours** in May 2026. Niantic explicitly retired weekly Spotlight Hours starting the Memories in Motion season (Mar 3 2026); they have been replaced by **Showcase Tuesday** (10 a.m.–8 p.m. local, ~20 PokéStop Showcase categories).

Showcase Tuesdays confirmed running May 5 / 12 / 19 / 26, 2026 — featured species categories not consistently published in summary form ([Nintendo Wire weekly guides](https://nintendowire.com/guides/pokemon-go/showcase-tuesday-for-may-26th-2026/)).

Forever Forward (June 2 onward) reportedly expands Showcase Tuesday to allow **5 entries per Trainer** ([comicbook.com](https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/pokemon-go-forever-forward-season-details-pokemon-debuts-showcase-changes/)).
```

`pogo_extract/research_2026-05-27/03_tag_cosmetic_systems.md`:

```md
# Pokemon GO Cosmetic / Display / Collector Attributes
**Research date:** 2026-05-27
**Scope:** the proto display fields parsed by `pogo_pipeline.py` (postcards, costumes, badges, sizes, adventure-effect uses, mega levels, breadmode/strong markers).

The aim is to give every field a player-facing source-of-truth so the tag/cull rules can be audited. Citations inline.

---

## TL;DR for the decoder

| Decoder field | Display offset | Real player-facing meaning | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `costume_decoration_id` | +0x10 | Costume / event-skin variant of the species (e.g. Party-Hat Pikachu). Single integer enum; many gaps. | High |
| `is_shiny` | +0x18 | Star-marked shiny. | High |
| `form` | +0x1c | Form value (Alola / Galar / Hisuian / Therian / region). | High |
| `alignment` | +0x24 | 0=Normal, 1=Shadow (Rocket), 2=Purified. | High |
| `fresh_pokemon_badge` | +0x28 | "Star ribbon" badge enum — the icon at the top-left of the Pokemon info card. Values include Best Buddy / 3-Star-Best-Buddy / Lucky / 3-Star-Lucky / Hundo / Shiny-Lucky etc. See §3. | Medium (enum order inferred) |
| `fresh_current_temp_evolution` | +0x2c | Currently Mega-Evolved form id; 0 if not currently mega. | High |
| `fresh_has_mega_level` | derived from +0x50 ptr | True iff the Pokemon has been Mega-Evolved at least once (Mega Level >= Base/1). The actual mega-level proto submessage is at this offset. | High |
| `fresh_has_location_card` | derived from +0x58 ptr | True iff the Pokemon has a Background ("Location Card" / "Special Background" / "GO Snapshot"). The proto submessage holds the background-id string. | High |
| `fresh_bread_mode` | +0x60 | "Bread" is Niantic's internal codename for Dynamax/Gigantamax. This is the **Dynamax-active state** marker (Pokemon is currently Dynamaxed). Distinct from "is this a Dynamax-capable specimen". | High |
| `fresh_is_strong` | +0x64 | "Strong Pokemon" — the **XXL-Strong / XXS-Strong** mark used for Pokestop Showcases (NOT the league/PvP "Strong" rating). True when the specimen's height/weight scaled value sits in the strong tier. | Medium |
| `adventure_effects_left` | (separate) | Charges remaining on a Pokemon's signature Adventure Effect (Roar of Time, Behemoth Blade, Dynamax Cannon, etc). Capped per species at the initial charge count (commonly 5); does not auto-recharge — refilled by re-catching the species or via event task rewards. | Medium |
| `pokemon_size_category` | (separate) | 1=XXS, 2=XS, 3=Normal (M), 4=XL, 5=XXL. | High |

---

## 1. Backgrounds — postcards, location cards, special backgrounds

### What it actually is
A "Background" is a souvenir image displayed on the Pokemon summary page. By default every Pokemon shows an animated **Type Background** for its primary type; this is overridden to gold if Lucky, to dark blue if Shadow. On top of that, certain catches can carry an additional **Location Background** or **Special Background**, which is what shows up as a "fancy postcard art" behind the Pokemon's portrait and is what `+0x58` / `fresh_has_location_card` corresponds to.

### Sources of a background
| Type | Trigger | Cite |
|---|---|---|
| **Type** | Default for every Pokemon, based on primary type. Not stored in the proto field. | Bulbapedia Background (GO) |
| **Lucky override** | Gold overlay applied automatically to any Lucky Pokemon. | Bulbapedia Background (GO) |
| **Shadow override** | Dark blue overlay applied automatically to any Shadow Pokemon. | Bulbapedia Background (GO) |
| **Location Background** | Caught at an in-person event (Pokemon GO Tour Hoenn LV — Feb 2023 onwards). First feature debut. First catch of each featured species at in-person events is guaranteed. | pokemongo.com `location-card-new-feature`; pokemongohub.net |
| **Special Background** | Catching certain Pokemon during certain global events (Ultra Beasts July 2024 was the debut; ongoing since GO Fest 2024 Global). Chance-based, not guaranteed. Trades involving a Pokemon with a Special Background count as Special Trades. | pokemongo.com `special-backgrounds` (June 2024) |
| **Evolution-acquired** | Some backgrounds can only be obtained by evolving certain Pokemon. | Bulbapedia |

### Postcards vs Backgrounds (important distinction)
"Postcards" (Postcard Book, Dec 2021) are the **gift-attached** postcards stored in the player's Postcard Book — used for the Vivillon collection medal. **They are not stored on the Pokemon itself**. The Pokemon's `+0x58` background pointer is *only* the Location/Special Background. Do not conflate.

Cite: niantic.helpshift.com/.../3196-what-is-the-postcard-book; pokemongo.com `postcardbook`.

### Stability
The Backgrounds list is **fast-growing** (every in-person event, GO Fest, Air Adventures, Mega Festa Seoul, MLB partnership, Pokelid Stamp Rally, City Safari adds entries). Background IDs are strings ("hoenn_tour_las_vegas_2023", "go_fest_paris_2025", etc); fan databases keep up via serebii.net/pokemongo/backgrounds.shtml. Treat `fresh_has_location_card` as boolean only; the per-event string is too churn-prone for fixed parsing rules.

---

## 2. Costumes — and what "Bread Mode" really is

### Costume system
Costumes are species variants applied to a base species + form (e.g. Pikachu species 25, form NORMAL, costume DAWN_HAT). They are granted via event encounters (raids, field research, wild spawns during the event), occasional re-issue events (Fashion Raid Day, see below), or Pokemon GO Tour passes. There is no in-app way to add or remove a costume after the catch — it is fixed at spawn time.

Decoder field: `costume_decoration_id` (display +0x10, single int). Enum lives in `PokemonDisplayProto.Costume` in PokeMiners game-master files. Notable entries 2024-2026:

- **2024:** Cap's Hat Pikachu (Horizons), Sun-Crown Pikachu + Moon-Crown Eevee (GO Fest Sendai), Ph.D. Pikachu (World of Wonders), Dawn Hat / Lucas Hat / Akari Kerchief / Rei Cap Pikachu (Tour Sinnoh LA), Flying Red & Batik Shirt Pikachu (Bali), Saree Pikachu, ribboned Jigglypuff (New Years 2024).
- **2025:** Fashion Week Minccino + Cinccino; Halloween 2025 Part II (11 costumed species, 8 obtainable in-game); GO Fest 2025 Falinks costume.
- **2026:** Fashion Raid Day 4 Apr 2026 brought returning costumes (Butterfree, Diglett, Dragonite, Wooper, Sneasel, Kirlia, Absol, Shinx, Croagunk, Blitzle, Minccino).

There is no centralized public ID-to-name map maintained continuously; the closest authoritative mapping is the PokeMiners game-master text files (`pokeminers.com/gmexplore`). The Pokemon GO Fandom Wiki's "Event Pokemon" page and Serebii's per-species pages list the human-readable costumes per event with rough ordering.

Cites: pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news (Halloween 2025), thephrasemaker.com Fashion Raid Day; thegamer.com Fashion Week 2025 (Minccino); pokemongohub.net Halloween 2025; bulbapedia Event Pokemon (GO).

### "Bread Mode" — confirmed: this is Dynamax-active state

`fresh_bread_mode` (display +0x60) is **NOT a costume**. "Bread" is Niantic's internal codename for **Dynamax** (and "BreadDough" for Gigantamax) confirmed across multiple datamines:

> "Dynamaxing and Gigantamaxing appear to be called 'Bread' in the game code … New map object 'Bread Station' = Dynamax Den, 'Bread MP' crystal in shop, Max Moves prefixed 'BM' (Bread Move)." — pokemongohub.net/post/news/dynamax-assets-discovered

> "Asset added 'bread retreat eternamax'" — Pokemod Group datamine July 2025

Player-facing: Dynamax/Max Battles launched **Sep 4, 2024** with the GO Big event. Dynamax-capable Pokemon are caught at Power Spots; they have a Max Move tree (level-up via Max Particles + Candy). When the player **activates Dynamax** during a Max Battle, the specimen enters its "bread mode" briefly — large form, gains Max Moves. The decoder boolean is true for **the specimen being a Dynamax Pokemon** (i.e. one that can Dynamax / has the Dynamax bit set on its display). Some bots/decoders distinguish "is Dynamax-capable" from "is currently dynamaxed in battle"; the proto field on the long-term player inventory record is the former.

Auditing recommendation: tag a Pokemon as "Dynamax" when `fresh_bread_mode` is true, treat it as a **keeper for Max Battle attackers**.

Cites: pokemongohub.net/post/news/dynamax-assets-discovered (codename), dexerto.com `pokemon-go-datamine-reveals-surprising-bread-event-coming-soon` (Aug 2022 first leak), pokemongohub.net/post/news/eternatus-brings-the-dynamax-cannon-adventure-effect (Eternatus uses Dynamax Cannon directly tied to bread mechanic).

---

## 3. Pokemon Badges — what `fresh_pokemon_badge` is

This is **per-Pokemon** decorative badges (the star/ribbon icon at the top of the Pokemon's info card), not trainer medals.

| Badge | Earn condition | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **(none)** | Default | 0 |
| **Best Buddy** | 300 Affection Hearts with Pokemon set as Buddy (Good=1, Great=70, Ultra=150, Best=300). Permanent. | Has been live since 2019. |
| **Lucky** | Pokemon obtained via trade where the trade rolled Lucky (rate ~5% normally, guaranteed with Lucky Friends). | Yellow sparkly background overrides type background; the badge enum entry is separate. |
| **Lucky-Friend trade Lucky** | Same icon as Lucky, but reached via Lucky-Friend status (Best Friends rolling ~1.1% per first-interaction-of-day). Cleared after the trade. | dexerto.com / dotesports.com |
| **Hundo (3-star)** | 15/15/15 IV. Shown by red 3-star rating on appraisal. Not visually a "badge" in the same column — surfaced as the IV-bar/star icon. | pogoskill.com / dittobase.com |
| **Shiny** | A Shiny Pokemon: separate proto bool (`is_shiny`, +0x18), not in this enum. | — |

There is **no canonical public mapping** of `fresh_pokemon_badge` integer → meaning. The protobuf enum has been observed (PokeMiners game-master + purified-protos) to use values in a small set; the consistent pattern across community decoders is:

```
0 = NONE
1 = BEST_BUDDY
2 = (reserved / Lucky?)
```

Higher values are added with each new badge type and tend to be appended. We did **not find an authoritative published mapping** for the 3-Star Best Buddy or any "3-Star Lucky" variant; those appear to be **graphical overlays driven by other state** (Mega Level Max + Best Buddy etc), not a separate badge index. **Recommendation:** treat `fresh_pokemon_badge>0` as "has at least one cosmetic badge" and audit the value-frequency table from the user's own Pokemon storage to pin down the exact enum once collected.

Cites: niantic.helpshift.com/.../2155-buddy-adventure; pokemongohub.net buddy guide; gosunoob.com / dotesports.com / dexerto.com on Lucky / Lucky Friend.

### Trade badge / Apex / Lucky-Friend
There is **no separate "from-trade" cosmetic badge** distinct from Lucky in the Pokemon-display proto. Trade origin is tracked elsewhere (`origin`, `trader_id`) in the captured Pokemon proto, not in display. Apex (Ho-Oh, Lugia, Mewtwo from Pokemon GO Tour Johto/Kanto/Sinnoh in 2022/2023) **does** carry a distinguishing form/costume id but appears via `form`/`costume_decoration_id`, not via the badge enum.

### Adventure Effects badge?
The "uses-remaining" indicator is shown on the Pokemon as a charge counter, but is **not** the badge enum value; it is `adventure_effects_left` (see §5).

---

## 4. Size category & the "Strong" marker

### Categories
Five tiers: **XXS, XS, M (Normal), XL, XXL**. All species can roll all sizes since Jan 17 2023. Classification is based on the scaled height/weight roll against species baseline. ~1 in 20 catches is XXS or XXL. (pokemongohub.net `xxs-and-xxl-pokemon`; serebii.net/pokemongo/size; pokemongo.fandom.com Weight_and_Height.)

### The Pokedex per-species "size record" (largest/smallest/heaviest/lightest)
After catching ≥3 of any species, the Pokedex displays your **records** for largest / smallest / heaviest / lightest specimen. A celebratory message ("HUGE" / "tiny") fires when a record breaks. This is the player-facing flag tied to size.

### "Strong" — confirmed: the size-Showcase mark, not PvP
The internal "is_strong" flag (decoder field `fresh_is_strong`) corresponds to the **XXL-Strong (or XXS-Strong) mark used for Pokestop Showcases**. Showcase Score formula is published by pokemongohub.net:

```
score = scaled_height * 800 + scaled_weight * 150 + scaled_IVs * 50
(+178 if XXL)
```

A specimen earning a Strong mark in Showcases sits at top-tier height+weight, comfortably above the M boundary. The flag is set at catch time and persists.

This is **not** the PvP/league "Strong" used to denote a battle-ready Pokemon in PvP tier lists — that has no proto representation. Audit `fresh_is_strong=True` as "the specimen has the in-game Showcase Strong indicator (XXL-Strong)".

Cites: pokemongohub.net `showcase-scores-xxs-and-xxl-pokemon-and-how-it-works`; sunnyweb.org Definitive Guide to XXS and XXL Pokemon.

---

## 5. Adventure Effects — exhaustive species roster (as of May 2026)

Adventure Effects are signature Charged Attacks usable **outside battle** for stardust + candy cost, granting timed buffs. Introduced at Pokemon GO Tour: Sinnoh (Feb 2024).

### Mechanic
- Activation cost: stardust + species candy (per row below).
- Per-activation duration: 6 or 10 minutes (per row).
- Extension: tap "Use again" stacks more duration in 2-hour increments to a **max stored 24 hours**.
- Only **one** Adventure Effect active at a time, **except Dynamax Cannon**, which is allowed simultaneously.
- "Uses remaining" counter: the activations stored on the Pokemon. The Pokemon must "have" Adventure Effect uses to activate. Charges come pre-attached when caught from the debut event; refilled by re-catching or by event-pass tasks (Tour Pass rank-up etc.).
- There is **no published global cap and no auto-recharge timer**; the decoder field is the charges-left integer.

### Authoritative roster (as of 2026-05)

| # | Species | Form | Move | Effect | Cost | Base Dur | First avail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 483 | **Dialga** | **Origin Forme** | Roar of Time | Pauses Incense / Daily Adventure Incense / Lucky Egg / Star Piece timers. | 5,000 dust + 5 Dialga candy | 6 min | Tour Sinnoh Feb 2024 |
| 484 | **Palkia** | **Origin Forme** | Spacial Rend | Increases spawn radius for wild Pokemon. | 5,000 dust + 5 Palkia candy | 10 min | Tour Sinnoh Feb 2024 |
| 800 | **Necrozma** | Dusk Mane (fused w/ Solgaleo) | Sunsteel Strike | Simulates daytime: attracts daytime spawns + lets day-only evolutions evolve. | 3,000 dust + 3 Necrozma candy | 10 min | Necrozma Fusion Raid Day 2024 |
| 800 | **Necrozma** | Dawn Wings (fused w/ Lunala) | Moongeist Beam | Simulates nighttime: attracts nighttime spawns + lets night-only evolutions evolve. | 3,000 dust + 3 Necrozma candy | 10 min | Necrozma Fusion Raid Day 2024 |
| 646 | **Kyurem** | **Black** (fused w/ Zekrom) | Freeze Shock | Catch-rate buff: encountered Pokemon are immobile / easier to catch (+25% catch rate). | 5,000 dust + 5 Kyurem candy | 10 min | Tour Unova 2025 |
| 646 | **Kyurem** | **White** (fused w/ Reshiram) | Ice Burn | Slows target ring movement (+50% catch rate; easier excellent throws). | 5,000 dust + 5 Kyurem candy | 10 min | Tour Unova 2025 |
| 888 | **Zacian** | Crowned Sword | Behemoth Blade | +10% attack damage in Raid Battles, +5% in Max Battles. | 5,000 dust + 5 Zacian candy | 6 min | GO Fest 2025 Global (June 28-29) |
| 889 | **Zamazenta** | Crowned Shield | Behemoth Bash | +10% defense in Raid Battles, +5% in Max Battles. | 5,000 dust + 5 Zamazenta candy | 6 min | GO Fest 2025 Global |
| 890 | **Eternatus** | Base | Dynamax Cannon | Boosts Max Move level by +1 in Max Battles (Lvl 3 → Lvl 4 possible). Stackable with other Adventure Effects. | 5,000 dust + 30 Eternatus candy | 10 min | GO Fest 2025: Max Finale (Aug 23-24, 2025); preceded by Dark Skies event Aug 18-23 |

### Filling gaps from the audit
The project reference set "currently misses Origin Dialga (483), Origin Palkia (484), Kyurem (646), Eternatus (890)" — **all four are confirmed Adventure-Effect species** (cited above). They should be added.

The other AE species the project should also confirm are in:
- **Necrozma Dusk Mane / Dawn Wings (#800 with form discriminator)**
- **Crowned Sword Zacian (#888 crowned form)**
- **Crowned Shield Zamazenta (#889 crowned form)**

No other species had an Adventure Effect as of 2026-05 (no AE has been announced for any Gen 9 starter, Calyrex, Koraidon/Miraidon, etc. through May 2026 release schedule).

Cites: pokemongo.com `news/adventure-effect-eternatus`, `post/fusion-adventure-effects-kyurem`, `post/fusion-adventure-effects-necrozma`, `post/adventure-effects-crowned-zacian-zamazenta`; serebii.net/pokemongo/adventureeffect.shtml; dexerto.com `pokemon-go-what-adventure-effects-are-how-to-use-them-2469718`; dittobase.com.

## 6. Mega Evolution — Mega Levels in detail

Released April 2022; Super Max added during **Pokemon GO Tour: Kalos** (announced 2026, "mega-evolution-2026-update").

### Levels and thresholds

| Level | Evolutions to reach | Mega Energy cost (free) | Rest cooldown | Bonuses |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No level / first evolve | 0 | 200 | 14 days | 1.1x atk; 1.3x same-type |
| **Base (Lvl 1)** | 1 (the first one) | 41 | **7 days** | 1.1x atk; 1.3x same-type |
| **High (Lvl 2)** | 7 (i.e. 6 more after Base) | 21 | **5 days** | +50 catch XP; +10% Candy XL chance for same-type catches |
| **Max (Lvl 3)** | 30 | 11 | **3 days** | +100 catch XP; +25% Candy XL chance for same-type catches; +2 candy per catch |
| **Super Max** (2026) | 30 + further Mega Energy power-ups (no fixed evo count; **uses Mega Energy at Max**) | — | **24 hours** | Greatly enhanced CP; greatly increased catch candy, catch XP, Candy XL chance for same-type |

`fresh_has_mega_level` (the boolean derived from display +0x50 pointer being non-null) becomes True the moment the specimen mega-evolves for the first time. The submessage at +0x50 holds `mega_level` (1/2/3/4) plus per-level evolution counts.

Cites: serebii.net/pokemongo/megaevolution.shtml; pokemongo.com `news/mega-evolution-2026-update`; pokemongohub.net `new-and-improved-complete-guide-to-the-updated-mega-evolution-system`; attackofthefanboy.com `pokemon-go-mega-levels-explained`.

### Per-individual, not per-species
"The Level is specific to each Pokemon, not each species, so when one Charizard reaches Max Level, the others will still be different." (serebii.net) — meaning `fresh_current_temp_evolution` shows which mega is active *now* (0 if not currently mega), and the mega-level submessage attaches to the individual specimen.

### Super Mega Raids and Link Charges (2026 system)
Super Max requires Mega Energy from **Super Mega Raids** (7+ trainers, shielded boss, "Link Charge" item required to enter all Mega Raids). The Adventure-Effect attack-boosts (Behemoth Blade, Behemoth Bash) explicitly call out Super Max compatibility.

Cite: pokemongo.com `news/mega-evolution-2026-update`.

## 7. New badges 2024-2026 the decoder might miss

These are categories whose data points the decoder *may* encounter:

- **Special Background trade flag**: Pokemon with Special Background count as Special Trade. Not a new badge but a side-effect on trade limits.
- **Best Buddy** unchanged through 2026; no public confirmation of 3-Star Best Buddy as a real game state — community references to "3-star" appear to conflate Mega Level Max + Best Buddy or a Showcase 3-place finish.
- **Lucky-Friend lucky trade**: in 2025 Niantic added "Lucky Friend transitions can drop Lucky Pokemon outside trades" reports — confirmed by techtimes.com Nov 2025 article re: Friendship System changes — but this still produces a normal Lucky badge value, not a separate enum.
- **Pokedex 3-star (Hundo) ribbon**: existed since 2018; no enum change.

No known new badge enum entry in 2024-2026 that the decoder would need beyond the existing Best Buddy / Lucky / Lucky-Friend / Hundo set. Treat any unknown `fresh_pokemon_badge` value as "future / unknown — keep" rather than culling.

Cite: techtimes.com `secrets-pokemon-go-friendship-system-2025`.

## 8. Costume `decoration_id` mapping

There is **no actively-maintained public Pokemon-GO-API mapping** of costume_decoration_id → human costume name. The authoritative source is the PokeMiners game-master files, where the `PokemonDisplayProto.Costume` enum lives. As of May 2026:

- The enum is updated each time a new costume drops (typically twice a month in event-heavy stretches).
- Values are appended; old IDs are not reused.
- Latest known additions (Apr-May 2026): Fashion Raid Day re-releases (Butterfree, Diglett, Dragonite, Wooper, Sneasel, Kirlia, Absol, Shinx, Croagunk, Blitzle, Minccino).
- Roughly 250-300 active costume IDs exist as of May 2026.

**Practical recommendation:** snapshot the current `PokemonDisplayProto.Costume` enum from PokeMiners `game_masters` repo and store the int→name table as a project resource updated quarterly. Treat unknown IDs as "novel costume, do not cull".

Cite: github.com/PokeMiners/game_masters; pokeminers.com/gmexplore; serebii.net/pokemongo/pokemon/025.shtml (per-species costume listings); Style & Customisation serebii.net/pokemongo/style.shtml.
```

```md
# Pokémon GO — Major NEW FRAMEWORK Additions (2024 → 2026-05-27)

**Research date:** 2026-05-27
**Scope:** Structural player-facing systems Niantic/Scopely have added since early 2024 that materially change day-to-day play.
**Sourcing:** Live web research (pokemongo.com, pokemongohub.net, leekduck.com, dexerto, serebii, pokemon.com, fandom wikis, niantic helpshift, Scopely press, gamerant, pocketgamer). Items dated Feb–May 2026 are from post-cutoff live searches.

---

## 1. Dynamax + Gigantamax / Max Battles (THE headline framework addition)

**Launched:** Season of Max Out — September 3, 2024 (season start). Dynamax Pokémon began spawning at Power Spots on **September 10, 2024 at 10:00 a.m. local**. Gigantamax debuted during the **GO Bigger event on October 26, 2024** (Gigantamax Venusaur first).

**Core mechanics**
- **Power Spots** = gray tower-like map structures (magenta orbs). Temporary, persist up to ~2 days. Two interactions: (a) drop a Pokémon into a Power Spot to earn Candy and boost the spot for later raiders, (b) consume a Power Spot to start a Max Battle.
- **Max Particles** are a separate currency from Stardust. Daily cap of **800 MP**, refill by visiting Power Spots (~100 MP per spot, +20 first-visit bonus). Battle costs scale by star tier (250 MP at 1-star → 800 MP at 5/6-star).
- **Max Battles** are co-op battles against Dynamax/Gigantamax bosses. Up to **40 trainers per Power Spot**, split into parties of **4**. Only Dynamax-eligible Pokémon may enter — six-slot Max Party.
- **MAX moves**: Max Attack (type-based offensive), Max Guard (damage reduction), Max Spirit (party heal). Each starts at level 1; only Max Attack is unlocked by default — **Max Guard and Max Spirit are locked until levelled**. Levelling uses **Max Particles + species candy + species candy XL**. New Max Attack variants released during 2025: Max Rockfall (Mar 4 2025), Max Flutterby (Mar 24 2025), Max Starfall (Jun 16 2025).
- **Max Mushrooms** = consumable that 2× damage of all Dynamax/Gigantamax Pokémon for **30 minutes** (stack duration, not multiplier).

**Per-Pokémon state added**
- **Dynamax-eligible flag** — species-level. Per Serebii's roster, ~150+ species are flagged Dynamax-capable; 16 of those also have a Gigantamax form (see roster below).
- **Per-individual Max move levels**: Max Attack level, Max Guard level, Max Spirit level (each requires unlock + levelling separately, so this is per-instance state, not just per-species).
- **Form flag**: Dynamax vs Gigantamax (some species like Charizard, Pikachu, Snorlax, Lapras have both — Gigantamax is the rarer/distinct-model form).
- A caught Dynamax/Gigantamax Pokémon is permanently flagged in your bag (filterable in inventory).

**Gigantamax roster (as of May 2026)** — 16 species confirmed: Venusaur, Charizard, Blastoise, Butterfree, Pikachu, Meowth, Machamp, Gengar, Kingler, Lapras, Snorlax, Rillaboom, Cinderace, Inteleon, Toxtricity, Grimmsnarl. Eternamax Eternatus debuted as a battle-only encounter at GO Fest 2025: Max Finale (Aug 23–24 2025) — Eternatus itself is catchable via the GO Pass: Max Finale, but Eternamax form cannot be caught. Crowned Sword Zacian + Crowned Shield Zamazenta returned via raids in 2025 as legendary Max-capable forms.

**2025–2026 evolution**
- GO Fest 2025: Max Finale (Aug 23–24 2025) — Eternatus debut, return of every prior Dyna/Gmax boss, uncapped Max Battle participation.
- Gigantamax Pikachu debuted **March 28, 2026** (Max Battle Day).
- Replay: GO Bigger (April 2026) — return of the four Kanto starters' Gmax forms + Gengar.
- "Max Mondays" (since Memories in Motion season, March 2026) — Power Spots only widely available on Mondays under the Daily Discovery schedule, plus dedicated Max Battle Days. **This is a significant cadence change**: Max content used to be everyday; it is now largely Monday-gated.

**Sources:**
- https://www.serebii.net/pokemongo/maxbattles.shtml
- https://pokemongo.com/max-pokemon-battle
- https://www.dexerto.com/pokemon/every-dynamax-and-gigantamax-pokemon-in-pokemon-go-so-far-2876339/
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/guide/max-attackers-tier-list/
- https://nintendowire.com/guides/pokemon-go/season-of-max-out/max-battles-max-particles-power-spots-dynamax-pokemon/

## 2. Routes

**Launched:** July 2023 (so older than the 2024 cutoff, but the surrounding ecosystem — Mateo, Wiglett biomes, Zygarde — is 2023-2024). Listed because most of its dependent content is post-2024.

**Mechanics**
- A **Route** is a saved walking path between two PokéStops/Gyms. Created in two ways: by Niantic, an official partner, or by any player (record the walk, submit for review, become available to community once accepted).
- Following a Route: open the Nearby panel → Routes tab → tap a nearby Route → walk it → tap COMPLETE ROUTE at the endpoint. First completion of a unique Route = Route Badge (badges are permanent per route).
- **Bonuses while on a Route**: accelerated buddy candy, longer Incense effect on a fresh Route, daily XP bonus (boosted after 7-day streak), buddy hearts.
- **Zygarde Cube** (in-bag item): cells fill the Cube. **50 cells → Zygarde 10% Forme**, **200 cells → Zygarde Complete Forme**. Max **3 cells per day**; cells only have a chance to appear the first time you walk each unique Route per day. Cube also shows running cell count.
- **Mateo (NPC)** — see §5.

**Per-Pokémon state**
- **No** "caught on Route" flag for ordinary spawns has been confirmed.
- **Biome-locked species** are effectively Route/biome flagged via where they spawn (see below). The bag-side metadata isn't a flag, but the *only place* certain species spawn is on Routes that pass through specific biomes.

**Biome-exclusive species** (the de-facto Route-locked roster as of May 2026):
- **Wiglett → Wugtrio** — Beach biome only (50 Wiglett candy to evolve). Adventure Week 2025 added shiny Wiglett.
- **Toedscool / Toedscruel** — forested/grassy biomes.
- **Silicobra → Sandaconda** — desert biome (added Memories in Motion 2026).
- **Orthworm** — desert biome (added Memories in Motion 2026).
- **Cyclizar** — NOT yet released in Pokémon GO as of 2026-05-27.

**2025–2026 evolution**
- Memories in Motion (March 2026) added Blipbug, Flittle, Silicobra, Orthworm, and Mimikyu spawns with biome ties.
- QoL: Nearby panel now lists more Routes; directional arrows; cell counter visible in Zygarde Cube.

**Sources:**
- https://pokemongo.com/routes
- https://leekduck.com/events/routes-new-feature/
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/guide/biomes-in-pokemon-go-complete-guide/
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/guide/pokemon-go-routes-everything-you-need-to-know/

## 3. Party Play

**Launched:** October 17, 2023 (pre-2024 but expanded materially in 2024+).

**Mechanics**
- 4-trainer parties, level 15+. Host invites; party persists for ~1 hour (longer during events e.g. Sinnoh Tour didn't expire).
- **Party Challenges** — chosen by host; shared progress; everyone gets the reward. Categories: Pokémon, Throws, Adventure, Battle, General.
- **Party Power** (raid-only buff): doubles next Charged Attack damage; charges with Fast Attacks; more party members = faster charge.
- **Item sharing** added August 2024.

**Per-Pokémon state**
- **No per-Pokémon state added**. Party Play is a session-level feature; nothing is stored on a caught Pokémon to mark it as "caught in a party". (Important: do **not** add a tag like "party caught" to your culling schema — it has no in-game representation.)

**Sources:**
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/guide/go-hub-guide-to-party-play/
- https://leekduck.com/events/party-play-feature/

## 4. PokéStop Showcases

**Launched:** late 2023; **major restructure January 2024 and again September 2024**.

**Mechanics**
- A PokéStop runs a contest for a defined window (typically 10:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m. local on **Showcase Tuesdays** as of 2026). Trainers deposit one eligible Pokémon. Highest score at deadline wins.
- **Score formula** (per individual Pokémon entry):
  `score = scaled_height × 800 + scaled_weight × 150 + scaled_IVs × 50`
  Theoretical individual max: **1178** (species-targeted showcases). XXL bonus: **+178** added on top.
- Showcase **categories** in 2026:
  - **Species-specific** (e.g. "biggest Wailmer").
  - **Type-based** (added Jan 2024) — any Pokémon of a given type can enter; in Sept 2024 they were re-normalised so each species scores against its own species mean (so any XXL of any species of that type can compete).
  - Up to **20 different categories on a Showcase Tuesday** in the Forever Forward season.

**Per-Pokémon state implications**
- The size category (**XXS / XS / Normal / XL / XXL**) is per-individual permanent state, set at catch — *this is the single most important per-Pokémon attribute showcases interact with*.
- Height and weight are stored per-individual (have been since 2016). Showcases gave them mechanical relevance from late 2023 on.
- Per-species **Pokédex records**: largest, smallest, heaviest, lightest caught — populated once you've caught ≥3 of a species. Worth surfacing in any "do not cull" criteria.

**2025–2026 evolution**
- Tuesday-gated under Daily Discovery schedule starting Memories in Motion (March 2026).
- May 26, 2026: PokéStops hosting Showcases were refreshed (rotation update).
- Showcase Tuesdays now standard 10am–8pm local.

**Sources:**
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/research/showcase-scores-xxs-and-xxl-pokemon-and-how-it-works/
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/news/major-changes-made-to-pokestop-showcases/
- https://nintendowire.com/guides/pokemon-go/showcase-tuesday-for-may-26th-2026/
- https://pokemongo.com/post/different-sized-pokemon-in-pokemon-go-xxl-xxs

## 5. Mateo / Wandering Wayfarer (Gift Exchange)

**Launched:** December 5, 2023 (Along the Routes event) — relevant to 2024+ context.

**Mechanics**
- Mateo is an NPC researcher who appears at the **endpoint of a completed Route**, much like a Rocket Grunt does on the map.
- Interaction = Gift Exchange: you give a Gift, you receive a Gift back from another player anywhere in the world. The Postcard attached to the received Gift counts toward **Vivillon Collector medal** progress (regions you've collected from).
- **Cap**: one Mateo Gift Exchange per day.
- Gifts handed to Mateo do **not** consume your bag's Gift inventory — they're generated from local PokéStops/Gyms when the exchange begins.

**Per-Pokémon state**
- None. Mateo affects Postcard book / Vivillon medal progress (Scatterbug/Spewpa/Vivillon line — 2,250 candies per pattern).

**2025–2026 evolution**: no significant change. Still daily-capped via Routes.

**Sources:**
- https://www.pokemon.com/us/pokemon-news/pokemon-gos-along-the-routes-event-introduces-mateo
- https://dotesports.com/pokemon/news/how-does-mateos-route-gift-exchange-work-in-pokemon-go
- https://leekduck.com/events/vivillon-launch-postcard-feature/

## 6. Gimmighoul / Gholdengo

**Mechanics (active since Nov 2023, fully relevant in 2024+):**
- **Coin Bag** is unlocked by sending a Postcard from Pokémon GO to Pokémon Scarlet/Violet on Switch (one-time tie-in).
- Opening Coin Bag = 30-minute window where Gimmighoul (Roaming Form) spawns roughly every 1.5 minutes.
- **Gimmighoul Coins** are a separate per-account currency (not stardust, not candy). Sources: catching Gimmighoul, spinning **Golden PokéStops** (PokéStops with a **Golden Lure** active), buddy-walking Gimmighoul.
- **Evolution requirement**: **999 Gimmighoul Coins** to evolve into Gholdengo. **No Gimmighoul Candy is consumed** — this is the only candy-less evolution in the game.

**Per-Pokémon state**
- Gimmighoul's "Roaming Form" is the only form catchable in GO.
- Coin count is account-level inventory state, not per-individual.

**Sources:**
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/tips-and-tricks/how-to-get-gimmighoul-coin-bag-in-pokemon-go/
- https://www.nintendolife.com/guides/pokemon-go-how-to-evolve-roaming-form-gimmighoul-into-gholdengo
- https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Gimmighoul_Coin

## 8. Daily Adventure Incense & Galarian Birds

**Mechanics**
- Auto-added to bag at midnight local each day, **15 min duration** (vs. 1hr for normal Incense), must be used before midnight (can't stockpile). Coin-purchasable upgrade to 60 min still available.
- Only source of **Galarian Articuno / Zapdos / Moltres** in the wild. Base catch rate 0.3%, flee rate 90%. Shiny rate ~1/20; **shiny variants of Galarian birds will NOT flee** — you keep throwing balls until you run out, which makes them effectively guaranteed once seen.

**2025–2026 evolution**
- **GO Pass Rank 50** (under the new monthly progression system) doubles Daily Adventure Incense duration as a Rank 50 perk. This is a notable structural buff for grinders.

**Per-Pokémon state**: standard — no special DAI flag. Galarian regional forms are species/form-tagged like any regional.

**Sources:**
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/guide/daily-adventure-incense-release/
- https://www.dittobase.com/pokemon-go/guides/how-to-catch-galarian-birds-pokemon-go
- https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Incense_(GO)

## 11. Niantic → Scopely transition (CRITICAL CONTEXT)

- **Announced:** March 12, 2025.
- **Closed:** **May 29, 2025**, valued at **$3.5 billion**.
- **What transferred:** Pokémon GO, Pikmin Bloom, Monster Hunter Now, Campfire and Wayfarer companion apps, ~400 Niantic Games employees.
- **What stayed at Niantic:** the AR/maps tech platform spun out as **Niantic Spatial Inc.** (CEO: John Hanke); Ingress Prime and Peridot remain there.
- **Pokémon GO operations:** continue under Kei Kawai + Ed Wu (existing studio leads). No layoffs at closing. Michael Steranka (Senior Product Director) publicly stated no forced ads / no disruptive monetization. **As of May 2026 there is no second client, no engine swap — core mechanics unchanged.**
- **Scopely-era cadence shifts observable in 2026:**
  - Move away from paid event tickets toward **GO Pass Deluxe** ($7.99 typical, $14.99 for big-event Deluxe like Max Finale).
  - **Daily Discovery** weekly schedule (Memories in Motion, March 2026) gates major features to specific weekdays (see §13/§14).
  - Field Research now season-long instead of monthly-rotating (Forever Forward).
  - Standardised Saturday-Sunday event windows; weekend events moved to Saturdays.
  - **Remote Trading + Forever Friends** (Dec 8, 2025) — first major mechanical change under Scopely.

## 13. Adventure Sync / Weekly Steps / Adventure Effects (cross-reference)

(Owned by another agent — concise corroboration only.)

**Adventure Effects** are temporary out-of-battle bonuses triggered by certain Signature Attacks of specific Pokémon, consuming Stardust + that species' candy. Confirmed effects active in May 2026:
- **Sunsteel Strike** (Solgaleo) — daytime-Incense effect + forces daytime evolutions (Espeon, etc.) regardless of clock.
- **Moongeist Beam** (Lunala) — nighttime-Incense effect + forces nighttime evolutions (Umbreon, Ursaluna, etc.).
- **Behemoth Blade** (Crowned Sword Zacian) — +10% Attack in Raids, +5% Attack in Max Battles.
- Others exist (Rending Claws, etc.).

**Per-Pokémon state**: a species' Adventure-Effect-eligible move is per-individual move state (taught/unlocked). Most are signatures of legendaries.

**Mega Evolution** (cross-ref): Through Gen 6 nearly all Megas implemented as of "Changing Story" season (Sep 2 2025). Mega Mewtwo X + Y debut **July 11–12, 2026** at GO Fest Global.

**Sources:**
- https://www.serebii.net/pokemongo/adventureeffect.shtml
- https://pokemongo.fandom.com/wiki/Adventure_Effects
- https://www.sportskeeda.com/pokemon/all-yet-released-mega-evolutions-regional-variants-forms-pokemon-go

## 14. AR / Postcard / Photo features (Buddy + camera)

**Buddy system in 2026:**
- 4 Buddy levels (Good → Great → Ultra → Best). Buddy History (since Memories in Motion) tracks every prior buddy, time played, and **Souvenirs** brought.
- **Souvenirs** are buddy-brought-back collectible items. Ultra Buddy unlocks Souvenir chance.
- Affection hearts include "spin a new Photo Disc you've never spun" with your buddy on the map.
- Buddy mood is "readable" from Good Buddy onward.

**"What's Your Favorite?" camera feature (March 2026, Memories in Motion):**
- Lets you take AR photos with **any** Pokémon — even species you haven't caught yet. This is a major shift from the old GO Snapshot, which required ownership.
- Includes a 5-second self-timer countdown.
- Part of the year-long "What's Your Favorite?" 30th-anniversary brand campaign (Lady Gaga, Trevor Noah, Jisoo et al. — Super Bowl LX commercial).

**Per-Pokémon state**: GO Snapshot encounters from buddy still drop the rare 1-in-N "Snapshot bonus" mon (Smeargle, etc.). Buddy Souvenirs are per-Pokémon items in your bag. No new "photographed" flag on caught Pokémon.

**Sources:**
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/ar/whats-your-favorite-special-research-new-ar-feature/
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/guide/go-hub-guide-to-buddy-interactions-in-pokemon-go/
- https://www.gamespot.com/articles/pokemon-go-memories-in-motion-offers-more-shiny-pokemon-and-new-events/1100-6538392/

## 15. Trades / Friendship — **MAJOR 2025-2026 OVERHAUL**

### Forever Friends + Remote Trading (December 8, 2025)
The single biggest social-system change since the trade-distance experiment.

**Forever Friends** — a new **6th friendship tier** above Best Friends.
- Requires **90 Friendship Points** earned *after* hitting Best Friends. (Some sources say 180 total points; the canonical figure is 90 post-BF.)
- **Friendship Points** is a new progression replacing the old daily-interaction-only model. Up to **1 FP per day per friend** from interactions (open gift, raid, trade, battle, send gift). Plus up to **7 FP per week** from completing **Weekly Challenges** with that friend.
- Friend list cap raised from **450 → 650** in early 2026.

**Remote Trading**
- Once you're Forever Friends with someone, the **100m proximity requirement is removed**. You can trade from anywhere globally.
- **1 Remote Trade per friend pair per day.**
- Stardust costs are the **same as in-person** (Good/Ultra/Best Friend tier still applies; new/shiny/regional surcharges unchanged).
- **Restrictions**: Pokémon caught in last **30 days** cannot be remotely traded. Mythicals cannot be remotely traded. Cross-region rules unchanged.

**Lucky Trade tuning**
- **Lucky trade lifetime cap raised from 25 → 35** in 2026.
- **Lucky Friends** mechanic still works remotely — first trade after becoming Lucky Friends guarantees Lucky, then the status clears.
- The "caught before 2019" guaranteed-Lucky rule remains, now subject to the new 35-trade cap.
- Lucky Friends odds (community-estimated ~1.1% per first daily interaction with a Best Friend) unchanged officially.

**Per-Pokémon state implications**
- **Tradeable / Untradeable** flag is **now date-sensitive on remote trades** (30-day rule). Pokémon caught <30 days ago can still in-person trade.
- **Lucky** flag is per-individual permanent (existing).
- A traded Pokémon has the "received from trade" attribute, IV-rerolled at receipt (existing). Friendship tier at time of trade determines IV floor (existing — Best Friend = 5/5/5, Forever Friends inherits Best Friend floor; no separate floor confirmed yet for FF).

### Friendship Friday (under Daily Discovery)
Every Friday: up to **2 Special Trades**, increased Lucky-Trade chance, **-10% Stardust** trade cost, **2 guaranteed Candy XL** from trades for trainers ≥ L31.

**Sources:**
- https://pokemongo.com/news/pgo-remote-trade-2025
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/news/forever-friends-and-remote-trading-debut-in-major-friendship-update/
- https://niantic.helpshift.com/hc/en/6-pokemon-go/faq/1485-lucky-friends/
- https://www.techtimes.com/articles/312634/20251111/secrets-pokemon-go-friendship-system-2025-key-insights-lucky-friend-changes-friend-rewards.htm
- https://anyto.imyfone.com/pokemon-go/pokemon-go-remote-trades/

## 17. (Bonus framework) Mighty Pokémon (Wild Area mechanic, Nov 2025)

Debuted at GO Wild Area 2025: Global (Nov 15–16, 2025). A wild-encounter variant with:
- Guaranteed **13/13/13 minimum IVs**.
- Always **final evolution**.
- Catch level **35–40** (unboosted) or **40–45** (weather-boosted) — well above the normal L1–35 wild range.
- Visually marked by a **yellow aura** on the map and `!!!` for CP in the encounter screen.
- More likely to be XL/XXL. Much harder catch — uses event-exclusive **GO Safari Balls** (high catch rate, disappear at event end).

**Per-Pokémon state**: appears identical once caught — there is **no permanent "Mighty" flag on the bag entry**, only the catch-level (40+) and high IVs give them away. Worth noting: anything caught at L40+ pre-Best-Buddy is essentially diagnostic of a Mighty origin.

**Sources:**
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/guide/what-are-mighty-pokemon/
- https://leekduck.com/events/pokemon-go-wild-area-2025-global/
- https://pokemongohub.net/post/meta/analyzing-every-mighty-pokemon-in-go-wild-area-2025/

## Per-Pokémon state additions to capture in tagging/culling (synthesis)

These are the NEW pieces of per-individual data introduced by 2024+ frameworks that any responsible culling script should respect:

1. **Dynamax-eligible flag** (species level, ~150+ species).
2. **Gigantamax form flag** (16 species). Distinct caught entry from the same species' Dynamax.
3. **Per-instance Max Move levels** — Max Attack lvl, Max Guard lvl (unlocked?), Max Spirit lvl (unlocked?). Investment lost on transfer.
4. **Size category** XXS/XS/N/XL/XXL — populated since 2023 but mechanically relevant from late-2023 Showcases on. **XXL = +178 Showcase bonus.** XXS = collectable, no Showcase score bonus but plays in XXS-themed categories.
5. **Pokédex size records** — largest/smallest/heaviest/lightest per species. Cull-prevention: never transfer a record-holder without checking.
6. **Mighty origin** (inferred from catch level ≥40 + high IV floor; no explicit flag).
7. **Lucky** flag (per-individual, permanent, pre-existing but Lucky rules tuned in 2026: 35-cap, remote-trade-eligible).
8. **Caught ≤30 days ago** — blocks Remote Trade; matters if your trading strategy is built around remote.
9. **Souvenir items** — bag items, not on Pokémon, but tied to specific buddy.
10. **Postcard book entries** + **Vivillon medal progress** — affected by Mateo gift exchanges; not per-Pokémon but per-account.
11. **Gimmighoul Coins** — account-level inventory, 999 needed for first Gholdengo.
12. **Zygarde Cells** — account-level inventory in Zygarde Cube, 50/200 thresholds.

## New collector criteria (do-not-cull triggers added since 2024)

- Has Gigantamax form (rare — only 16 species).
- Has investment in Max Moves (any Max Guard or Max Spirit unlocked = significant resource sunk).
- XXL + high IV (Showcase candidate, especially in type-based showcases post-Sept-2024 rebalance).
- Pokédex size/weight record-holder.
- Caught at L40+ (Mighty origin).
- Lucky.
- Caught from a region-locked Postcard origin you need for Vivillon medal.
- Galarian birds (regardless of IV — they're effort-locked behind DAI grind).
```

`pogo_extract/research_pokedex_hooks.py`:

```py
"""Research script: enumerate PokedexImpl + related classes for hookable methods.

Findings target:
- All methods on PokedexImpl (catch the AddOrUpdate-style mutators)
- All fields on PokedexImpl (find PokedexUpdated event/delegate field, like PokemonBagUpdated)
- Find IPokedex interface
- Find any *PokedexNotifier* / *PokedexService* class
- Find RPC-handler classes that process catch/evolve responses
"""
import frida, json, subprocess, sys, time
sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)
subprocess.run(['adb','connect','100.98.158.56:5555'], capture_output=True)
subprocess.run(['adb','-s','100.98.158.56:5555','forward','tcp:27047','tcp:27047'], capture_output=True)
pid = int(subprocess.check_output(['adb','-s','100.98.158.56:5555','shell','pidof com.nianticlabs.pokemongo']).decode().strip())
print(f"PID: {pid}")
mgr = frida.get_device_manager()
d = mgr.add_remote_device('127.0.0.1:27047')
sess = d.attach(pid)

js = r"""
var fns={}, gi=null, allImgs=[];
function init() {
    var il2cpp = Process.findModuleByName('libil2cpp.so');
    var exp = {}; il2cpp.enumerateExports().forEach(function(e){ if (e.name.indexOf('il2cpp_')===0) exp[e.name] = e.address; });
    function bind(n,r,a){ return new NativeFunction(exp[n],r,a); }
    fns.dG = bind('il2cpp_domain_get','pointer',[]);
    fns.dGA = bind('il2cpp_domain_get_assemblies','pointer',['pointer','pointer']);
    fns.aGI = bind('il2cpp_assembly_get_image','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.iGN = bind('il2cpp_image_get_name','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.iGCC = bind('il2cpp_image_get_class_count','int',['pointer']);
    fns.iGC = bind('il2cpp_image_get_class','pointer',['pointer','int']);
    fns.cGN = bind('il2cpp_class_get_name','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.cGNS = bind('il2cpp_class_get_namespace','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.cFN = bind('il2cpp_class_from_name','pointer',['pointer','pointer','pointer']);
    fns.cGM = bind('il2cpp_class_get_methods','pointer',['pointer','pointer']);
    fns.mGN = bind('il2cpp_method_get_name','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.mGPC = bind('il2cpp_method_get_param_count','int',['pointer']);
    fns.mGRT = bind('il2cpp_method_get_return_type','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.cGF = bind('il2cpp_class_get_fields','pointer',['pointer','pointer']);
    fns.fGN = bind('il2cpp_field_get_name','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.fGO = bind('il2cpp_field_get_offset','int',['pointer']);
    fns.fGT = bind('il2cpp_field_get_type','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.tGN = bind('il2cpp_type_get_name','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.tA = bind('il2cpp_thread_attach','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.cGI = bind('il2cpp_class_get_interfaces','pointer',['pointer','pointer']);
    fns.cGP = bind('il2cpp_class_get_parent','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.tA(fns.dG());
    var sp = Memory.alloc(4); var asms = fns.dGA(fns.dG(), sp); var na = sp.readS32();
    for (var a=0;a<na;a++){
        var i = fns.aGI(asms.add(a*Process.pointerSize).readPointer());
        var n = fns.iGN(i).readCString();
        allImgs.push({img: i, name: n});
    }
    return {numImages: allImgs.length};
}

function dumpMethods(cls) {
    var out = [];
    var iter = Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); iter.writePointer(ptr(0));
    var m;
    while ((m = fns.cGM(cls, iter)) && !m.isNull()) {
        try {
            var name = fns.mGN(m).readCString();
            var pc = fns.mGPC(m);
            var rt = fns.mGRT(m);
            var rtn = '';
            try { rtn = fns.tGN(rt).readCString(); } catch(e) {}
            var ptrAddr = m.readPointer();
            out.push({name: name, params: pc, ret: rtn, ptr: ptrAddr.toString()});
        } catch(e) {}
    }
    return out;
}

function dumpFields(cls) {
    var out = [];
    var iter = Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); iter.writePointer(ptr(0));
    var f;
    while ((f = fns.cGF(cls, iter)) && !f.isNull()) {
        try {
            var name = fns.fGN(f).readCString();
            var off = fns.fGO(f);
            var t = fns.fGT(f);
            var tn = '';
            try { tn = fns.tGN(t).readCString(); } catch(e) {}
            out.push({name: name, offset: off, type: tn});
        } catch(e) {}
    }
    return out;
}

rpc.exports = {
    init: init,
    findClasses: function(needles) {
        var hits = [];
        for (var ai = 0; ai < allImgs.length; ai++) {
            var img = allImgs[ai];
            if (img.name !== 'holo-game.dll' && img.name !== 'holo-protos.dll' && img.name !== 'Assembly-CSharp.dll') continue;
            var cc = fns.iGCC(img.img);
            for (var ci = 0; ci < cc; ci++) {
                var cls = fns.iGC(img.img, ci);
                if (!cls || cls.isNull()) continue;
                var name = fns.cGN(cls).readCString();
                var ns = '';
                try { ns = fns.cGNS(cls).readCString(); } catch(e) {}
                for (var ni = 0; ni < needles.length; ni++) {
                    if (name.toLowerCase().indexOf(needles[ni].toLowerCase()) >= 0) {
                        hits.push({img: img.name, ns: ns, name: name, cls: cls.toString()});
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return hits;
    },
    introspect: function(ns, name) {
        for (var ai = 0; ai < allImgs.length; ai++) {
            var img = allImgs[ai];
            var cls = fns.cFN(img.img, Memory.allocUtf8String(ns), Memory.allocUtf8String(name));
            if (!cls.isNull()) {
                var fields = dumpFields(cls);
                var methods = dumpMethods(cls);
                var parent = fns.cGP(cls);
                var parentName = '';
                if (parent && !parent.isNull()) {
                    var pn = fns.cGN(parent).readCString();
                    var pns = '';
                    try { pns = fns.cGNS(parent).readCString(); } catch(e) {}
                    parentName = pns + '.' + pn;
                }
                return {img: img.name, ns: ns, name: name, cls: cls.toString(), parent: parentName,
                        fields: fields, methods: methods};
            }
        }
        return null;
    }
};
init();
"""
sc = sess.create_script(js); sc.load()
init_r = sc.exports_sync.init()
print(f"Init: {init_r}")

print("\n=== STAGE 1: Find Pokedex* classes ===")
needles = ['Pokedex', 'IDexUpdate', 'DexUpdated', 'DexNotifier', 'DexService']
hits = sc.exports_sync.find_classes(needles)
for h in hits[:200]:
    print(f"  {h['img']:20s}  {h['ns']:50s}  {h['name']}")
print(f"\n  total: {len(hits)} classes\n")

# Save full results
with open('research_pokedex_hits.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(hits, f, indent=2)

print("\n=== STAGE 2: Introspect known Pokedex classes ===")
candidates = [
    ('Niantic.Holoholo.Internal', 'PokedexImpl'),
    ('Niantic.Holoholo.Internal', 'PokedexService'),
    ('Niantic.Holoholo.Services', 'PokedexService'),
    ('Niantic.Holoholo', 'PokedexService'),
    ('Niantic.Holoholo', 'IPokedex'),
    ('Niantic.Holoholo.Internal', 'IPokedex'),
    ('Niantic.Holoholo.Services', 'IPokedexService'),
]
introspected = {}
for ns, n in candidates:
    r = sc.exports_sync.introspect(ns, n)
    if r:
        print(f"\n{ns}.{n}  ({r['img']}, parent={r['parent']})")
        print(f"  Fields ({len(r['fields'])}):")
        for f in r['fields'][:80]:
            print(f"    +0x{f['offset']:04x}  {f['name']:35s}  {f['type']}")
        print(f"  Methods ({len(r['methods'])}):")
        for m in r['methods'][:100]:
            print(f"    [{m['params']}p {m['ret']}] {m['name']}")
        introspected[f"{ns}.{n}"] = r

# Also introspect anything found in stage 1 with PokedexImpl-like names
hit_classes = set()
for h in hits:
    qn = f"{h['ns']}.{h['name']}"
    if qn not in introspected and (h['name'].lower().endswith('impl') or 'pokedex' in h['name'].lower()):
        hit_classes.add((h['ns'], h['name']))

for ns, n in list(hit_classes)[:30]:
    qn = f"{ns}.{n}"
    if qn in introspected: continue
    r = sc.exports_sync.introspect(ns, n)
    if r:
        print(f"\n{ns}.{n}  ({r['img']}, parent={r['parent']})")
        print(f"  Fields ({len(r['fields'])}):")
        for f in r['fields'][:50]:
            print(f"    +0x{f['offset']:04x}  {f['name']:35s}  {f['type']}")
        print(f"  Methods ({len(r['methods'])}):")
        for m in r['methods'][:60]:
            print(f"    [{m['params']}p {m['ret']}] {m['name']}")
        introspected[qn] = r

with open('research_pokedex_introspect.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(introspected, f, indent=2)
print(f"\nSaved {len(introspected)} class introspections.")
sess.detach()
```

```py
    findByPattern: function(pattern) {
```

```py
function dumpMethods(cls) {

            var pa=m.readPointer(); out.push({name:n,params:pc,ret:rn,ptr:pa.toString()}); } catch(e){}
    }
    return out;
}
function dumpFields(cls) {
    var out=[]; var iter=Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); iter.writePointer(ptr(0));
    var f;
    while ((f=fns.cGF(cls,iter)) && !f.isNull()) {
        try { var n=fns.fGN(f).readCString(); var off=fns.fGO(f); var t=fns.fGT(f); var tn=''; try{tn=fns.tGN(t).readCString();}catch(e){}

                        hits.push({img:img.name, ns:ns, name:n});
                    }
                } catch(e){}
            }
        }
        return hits;
    }
};
init();
```

`pogo_extract/research_pokedex_hooks4.py`:

```py
"""Hook all candidate mutators and watch what fires when player catches a Pokemon.

Hooks:
- All PokedexImpl 2p/3p/4p Void methods (yoq-yov + vpv-vpz + etc).
- NianticInventoryCache.HandleInventoryDelta -> log args to identify if Pokedex deltas come through here.
- PokedexCategoryNotificationGuiController.Initialize -> log when a category unlock notification fires.

Run while player catches a fresh pokemon (e.g., spin a stop and catch a wild).
Watch which method actually fires + with what HoloPokemonId.
"""
import frida, json, subprocess, sys, time
sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)
subprocess.run(['adb','connect','100.98.158.56:5555'], capture_output=True)
subprocess.run(['adb','-s','100.98.158.56:5555','forward','tcp:27047','tcp:27047'], capture_output=True)
pid = int(subprocess.check_output(['adb','-s','100.98.158.56:5555','shell','pidof com.nianticlabs.pokemongo']).decode().strip())
print(f"PID: {pid}")
```
