```py
    var svcCls = fns.cFN(gi, Memory.allocUtf8String('Niantic.Holoholo.Tagging'), Memory.allocUtf8String('TaggingRpcService'));
    function hookAll(cls, label) {
        var iter = Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); iter.writePointer(ptr(0));
        var m;
        while ((m = fns.cGM(cls, iter)) && !m.isNull()) {
            try { var addr = m.readPointer(); if (addr.isNull()) continue;
                Interceptor.attach(addr, {
                    onEnter: function(args) {
                        if (label === 'bag' && !bagInst) { bagInst = args[0].toString(); send({type:'h', msg:'bag '+bagInst}); }
                        if (label === 'svc' && !svcInst) { svcInst = args[0].toString(); send({type:'h', msg:'svc '+svcInst}); }
                    }
                });
            } catch(e) {}
        }
    }
    hookAll(bagCls, 'bag'); hookAll(svcCls, 'svc');
}
rpc.exports = { setup: function() { init(); return {ok:true}; }, get: function() { return {bag: bagInst, svc: svcInst}; } };

hs = sess.create_script(hook_js)
def on(m, data):

    if isinstance(p, dict) and 'msg' in p: print(f"  {p['msg']}")

if not SVC:

    scan_js = """
    rpc.exports = {
        scan: function() {
            var il2cpp = Process.findModuleByName('libil2cpp.so');
            var exp = {}; il2cpp.enumerateExports().forEach(function(e){ if (e.name.indexOf('il2cpp_')===0) exp[e.name] = e.address; });
            function bind(n,r,a){ return new NativeFunction(exp[n],r,a); }
            var dG=bind('il2cpp_domain_get','pointer',[]);
            var dGA=bind('il2cpp_domain_get_assemblies','pointer',['pointer','pointer']);
            var aGI=bind('il2cpp_assembly_get_image','pointer',['pointer']);
            var iGN=bind('il2cpp_image_get_name','pointer',['pointer']);
            var cFN=bind('il2cpp_class_from_name','pointer',['pointer','pointer','pointer']);
            var cGM=bind('il2cpp_class_get_methods','pointer',['pointer','pointer']);
            var mGN=bind('il2cpp_method_get_name','pointer',['pointer']);
            var rI=bind('il2cpp_runtime_invoke','pointer',['pointer','pointer','pointer','pointer']);
            var tA=bind('il2cpp_thread_attach','pointer',['pointer']); tA(dG());
            var sp=Memory.alloc(4); var asms=dGA(dG(),sp); var na=sp.readS32();
            var gi=null;
            for (var a=0;a<na;a++){ var i=aGI(asms.add(a*Process.pointerSize).readPointer()); if (iGN(i).readCString()==='holo-game.dll'){gi=i;break;} }
            var svcCls=cFN(gi, Memory.allocUtf8String('Niantic.Holoholo.Tagging'), Memory.allocUtf8String('TaggingRpcService'));
            var iter=Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); iter.writePointer(ptr(0));
            var m, gnt=null;
            while ((m = cGM(svcCls, iter)) && !m.isNull()) {
                if (mGN(m).readCString() === 'get_NumberOfTags') gnt = m;

            var hits = [];
            Process.enumerateRanges({protection:'rw-'}).forEach(function(r){
                if (r.size > 0x10000000 || hits.length > 10) return;
                var p = r.base; var end = r.base.add(r.size);
                while (p.compare(end) < 0) {
                    try {
                        if (p.readPointer().equals(svcCls)) {
                            var exc = Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); exc.writePointer(ptr(0));
                            var ret = rI(gnt, p, ptr(0), exc);
                            if (exc.readPointer().isNull()) {
                                var n = ret.add(0x10).readS32();
                                if (n >= 12 && n < 50) { hits.push({addr: p.toString(), tags: n}); if (hits.length > 5) break; }
                            }
                        }
                    } catch(e) {}
                    p = p.add(8);
                }
            });
            return {hits: hits};
        }
    };
```

```py
var fns={}; var bagInst=null, svcInstHook=null; var bagCls=null, svcCls=null, gi=null;
function initIL2() {
    var il2cpp = Process.findModuleByName('libil2cpp.so');
    var exp = {}; il2cpp.enumerateExports().forEach(function(e){ if (e.name.indexOf('il2cpp_')===0) exp[e.name] = e.address; });
    function bind(n,r,a){ return new NativeFunction(exp[n],r,a); }
    fns.dG=bind('il2cpp_domain_get','pointer',[]); fns.dGA=bind('il2cpp_domain_get_assemblies','pointer',['pointer','pointer']);
    fns.aGI=bind('il2cpp_assembly_get_image','pointer',['pointer']); fns.iGN=bind('il2cpp_image_get_name','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.cFN=bind('il2cpp_class_from_name','pointer',['pointer','pointer','pointer']); fns.cGM=bind('il2cpp_class_get_methods','pointer',['pointer','pointer']);
    fns.mGN=bind('il2cpp_method_get_name','pointer',['pointer']);
    fns.cMN=bind('il2cpp_class_get_method_from_name','pointer',['pointer','pointer','int']);
    fns.rI=bind('il2cpp_runtime_invoke','pointer',['pointer','pointer','pointer','pointer']);
    fns.tA=bind('il2cpp_thread_attach','pointer',['pointer']); fns.tA(fns.dG());
    var sp = Memory.alloc(4); var asms = fns.dGA(fns.dG(), sp); var na = sp.readS32();
    for (var a=0;a<na;a++){ var i=fns.aGI(asms.add(a*Process.pointerSize).readPointer()); if (fns.iGN(i).readCString()==='holo-game.dll'){ gi=i; break; } }
    bagCls = fns.cFN(gi, Memory.allocUtf8String('Niantic.Holoholo.Internal'), Memory.allocUtf8String('PokemonBagImpl'));
    svcCls = fns.cFN(gi, Memory.allocUtf8String('Niantic.Holoholo.Tagging'), Memory.allocUtf8String('TaggingRpcService'));
}

rpc.exports = {
    setup: function() {
        initIL2();
        // Hook only a few key methods per class to avoid overloading
        function hookKey(cls, names, label) {
            var iter = Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); iter.writePointer(ptr(0));
            var m, found = 0;
            while ((m = fns.cGM(cls, iter)) && !m.isNull()) {
                var nm = fns.mGN(m).readCString();
                if (names.indexOf(nm) >= 0) {
                    try {
                        var addr = m.readPointer();
                        if (addr.isNull()) continue;
                        Interceptor.attach(addr, {
                            onEnter: function(args) {
                                if (label === 'bag' && !bagInst) { bagInst = args[0].toString(); send({type:'h', msg:'bag '+bagInst}); }
                                if (label === 'svc' && !svcInstHook) { svcInstHook = args[0].toString(); send({type:'h', msg:'svc '+svcInstHook}); }
                            }
                        });
                        found++;
                    } catch(e) {}
                }
            }
            return found;
        }
        var n1 = hookKey(bagCls, ['get_AllPokemon','get_Count','get_AllPokemonProtos','GetPokemonByUid'], 'bag');
        var n2 = hookKey(svcCls, ['GetEnabledFilter','get_NumberOfTags','GetCachedTagToPokemonBindingForIndex','GetAllTags','SetPokemonTags','UpdateTagsForFilter'], 'svc');
        send({type:'h', msg:'hooked bag='+n1+' svc='+n2});
        return {ok:true};
    },
    get: function() { return {bag: bagInst, svc: svcInstHook}; },
    scanSvcChunk: function(startHi, sizeBytes) {
        var iter = Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); iter.writePointer(ptr(0));
        var m, gnt = null;
        while ((m = fns.cGM(svcCls, iter)) && !m.isNull()) {
            if (fns.mGN(m).readCString() === 'get_NumberOfTags') gnt = m;
        }
        var hits = [];
        var startAddr = ptr(startHi);
        var endAddr = startAddr.add(sizeBytes);
        // Limit which ranges to scan based on overlap with [startAddr, endAddr]
        Process.enumerateRanges({protection:'rw-'}).forEach(function(r){
            if (hits.length > 10) return;
            var rEnd = r.base.add(r.size);
            if (r.base.compare(endAddr) >= 0 || rEnd.compare(startAddr) <= 0) return;
            var p = r.base.compare(startAddr) > 0 ? r.base : startAddr;
            var e = rEnd.compare(endAddr) < 0 ? rEnd : endAddr;
            while (p.compare(e) < 0 && hits.length < 10) {
                try {
                    if (p.readPointer().equals(svcCls)) {
                        var exc = Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); exc.writePointer(ptr(0));
                        var ret = fns.rI(gnt, p, ptr(0), exc);
                        if (exc.readPointer().isNull()) {
                            var n = ret.add(0x10).readS32();
                            if (n >= 12 && n < 50) hits.push({addr: p.toString(), tags: n});
                        }
                    }
                } catch(e2) {}
                p = p.add(8);
            }
        });
        return {hits: hits};
    },
    findProtos: function(bagAddr, uids) {
        var ga = fns.cMN(bagCls, Memory.allocUtf8String('get_AllPokemon'), 0);
        var exc = Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize); exc.writePointer(ptr(0));
        var values = fns.rI(ga, ptr(bagAddr), ptr(0), exc);
        var lhm = values.add(0x10).readPointer();
        var list = lhm.add(0x18).readPointer();
        var head = list.add(0x10).readPointer();
        var count = list.add(0x18).readS32();
        var wanted = {}; for (var i=0;i<uids.length;i++) wanted[uids[i]] = true;
        var found = {}; var node = head; var iters = 0;
        while (node && !node.isNull() && iters < count + 200) {
            try {
                var key = node.add(0x28).readU64().toString();
                if (wanted[key]) found[key] = node.add(0x30).readPointer().toString();
                var next = node.add(0x18).readPointer();
                if (next.isNull() || next.equals(head)) break;
                node = next;
            } catch(e) { break; }
            iters++;
        }
        return {found: found};
    }
};
"""
sc = sess.create_script(combined_js)
def on(m, data):
    p = m.get('payload',{})
    if isinstance(p, dict) and 'msg' in p: print(f"  {p['msg']}")
```

`pogo_extract/untag_user_tagged.py`:

```py
"""URGENT: Untag CLAUDE_TX from any pokemon that already has user-tags (GMAX, DMAX, etc.)."""
import frida, sqlite3, json, time
mgr = frida.get_device_manager()
d = mgr.add_remote_device("127.0.0.1:27047")
sess = d.attach(d.enumerate_processes()[0].pid)
script = sess.create_script(open("bulk_tag.js","r",encoding="utf-8").read() + """
rpc.exports.readProtoUid = function(ptrStr) {
    try {
        var p = ptr(ptrStr);
        return {lo: p.add(32).readS32(), hi: p.add(36).readS32()};
    } catch(e) { return {err: e.message}; }
};
""")
script.on("message", lambda m, data: None)
script.load()
script.exports_sync.init_status()
script.exports_sync.index_pokemon()
real = "0x71bed7fe80"
ftid = script.exports_sync.find_tag_id_by_name(real, "CLAUDE_TX")
tag_proto = ftid["tagProtoAddr"]

# Get all user-tagged UIDs
TARGETS = ["D-Max","G-MAX","Mega","MegaHundos","Hundos","Shinyyy","TeamEevee","0-15-15","UL","Location Card","U","Trade","Nundos","Traded","Trade to Osiris","HUUUGE"]
listing = script.exports_sync.list_all_tags(real)
tag_idx_by_name = {}
for t in listing.get("tags", []):
    names = []
    def walk(x):
        if isinstance(x, dict):
            for k,v in x.items():
                if 'str' in k.lower() and isinstance(v,str) and v.strip() and len(v)<60: names.append(v)
                else: walk(v)
        elif isinstance(x, list):
            for y in x: walk(y)
    walk(t)
    if names: tag_idx_by_name[names[0]] = t.get("i")

user_tagged_uids = set()
for tag_name in TARGETS:
    if tag_name not in tag_idx_by_name: continue
    binding = script.exports_sync.get_pokemon_for_tag(real, tag_idx_by_name[tag_name])
    if not binding.get("ok"): continue
    for k, v in binding.get("dump", {}).items():
        if k.endswith("_listish") and isinstance(v, dict) and v.get("count", 0) > 0:
            for s in v.get("sample", []):
                pi = int(s["asI64"])
                if pi < 0: pi += 2**64
                u = script.exports_sync.read_proto_uid(hex(pi))
                if u.get("err"): continue
                lo = u["lo"] & 0xFFFFFFFF
                hi = u["hi"] & 0xFFFFFFFF
                full = (hi << 32) | lo
                if full >= 2**63: full -= 2**64
                user_tagged_uids.add(full)
            break
print(f"Total user-tagged pokemon: {len(user_tagged_uids)}")

# Cross-check with TRANSFER list
conn = sqlite3.connect("pokemon.db")
c = conn.cursor()
c.execute("SELECT uid, uid_hex, species_name, cp, iv_pct FROM pokemon WHERE cull_decision='TRANSFER'")
transfers = c.fetchall()
conn.close()
to_untag = [(uid, uid_hex, sp, cp, iv) for uid, uid_hex, sp, cp, iv in transfers if uid in user_tagged_uids]
print(f"Conflicts to untag: {len(to_untag)}")

# Untag each
untagged = 0
failed = 0
for uid, uid_hex, sp, cp, iv in to_untag:
    low = uid & 0xFFFFFFFF; high = (uid >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    if low > 0x7FFFFFFF: low -= 0x100000000
    if high > 0x7FFFFFFF: high -= 0x100000000
    p = script.exports_sync.find_pokemon_proto(low, high)
    if not p.get("ok"):
        failed += 1; continue
    r = script.exports_sync.bulk_untag_one(real, p["ptr"], tag_proto)
    if r.get("ok"):
        untagged += 1
    else:
        failed += 1
    if (untagged + failed) % 30 == 0:
        print(f"  progress: ok={untagged} failed={failed}")
    time.sleep(0.3)
print(f"\nFinal: untagged={untagged} failed={failed}")
sess.detach()
```

```py
Uses bulk_tag.js which has bulkUntagOne. Fresh Frida session.

    p = m.get("payload",{})
    if isinstance(p,dict):
        msg = p.get("msg","")
        if "captured this @" in msg:
            captured.append(msg.split("@")[1].strip().split(" ")[0])

script.exports_sync.hook_for_real_instance(180)

    time.sleep(1)
    try:
        cap = script.exports_sync.get_captured()
        if cap.get("captured"):
            real = list(cap["captured"].keys())[0]
            print(f"captured: {real}")
            break
    except: pass
    if i % 15 == 0 and i > 0:
        print(f"  still waiting... {i}/180s")
if not real:
    print("FAILED to capture real instance")
    exit(1)

    uid = t['uid']
    low = uid & 0xFFFFFFFF; high = (uid >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    if low > 0x7FFFFFFF: low -= 0x100000000
    if high > 0x7FFFFFFF: high -= 0x100000000

        fail_log.append({'uid_hex': t['uid_hex'], 'reason': 'find_proto_failed', 'species': t.get('species')})
        continue
    success = False
    last_err = None

            r = script.exports_sync.bulk_untag_one(real, p["ptr"], tag_proto)
            if r.get("ok"):

                success = True
                break
            else:
                last_err = r
        except Exception as e:
            last_err = str(e)
        time.sleep(0.5)
    if not success:
        fail += 1
        fail_log.append({'uid_hex': t['uid_hex'], 'species': t.get('species'), 'err': str(last_err)})
    if (ok+fail) % 20 == 0:
        print(f"  progress: ok={ok} fail={fail} ({ok+fail}/{len(targets)})")
    time.sleep(0.25)

print(f"\nFinal: untagged={ok} failed={fail}")
if fail_log:
    with open('untag_v3_fail.json', 'w') as f:
        json.dump(fail_log, f, indent=2)
    print(f"Wrote untag_v3_fail.json")
sess.detach()
```

```py
                        if (label === 'svc' && !svcInst) { svcInst = args[0].toString(); send({type:'h', msg:'svc '+svcInst}); }
                    }

            } catch(e) {}
        }
    }

        var values = rI(ga, inst, ptr(0), exc);

                var next = node.add(0x18).readPointer();

"""
```

```py
POGO_LAUNCH_MS = 1467590400000

print("Loading pokemon_v3.json + db...")

    raw = p.get('raw_proto', '')
    if len(raw) >= 1024:
        all_bytes.append(bytes.fromhex(raw))
N = len(all_bytes)

# UIDs
all_uids = [struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0] for bs in all_bytes]

conn = sqlite3.connect('pokemon.db')
c = conn.cursor()

def signed_to_unsigned(v):
    return v if v >= 0 else v + (1 << 64)

uid_to_idx = {}
for i, u in enumerate(all_uids):
    uid_to_idx[u] = i

# Build subsets
def db_idx_set(where_clause):
    rows = c.execute(f"SELECT uid FROM pokemon WHERE {where_clause}").fetchall()
    s = set()
    for (uid_signed,) in rows:
        u = signed_to_unsigned(uid_signed)
        if u in uid_to_idx:
            s.add(uid_to_idx[u])
    return s

s_hatched = db_idx_set("is_hatched_from_egg=1")
s_traded = db_idx_set("is_traded=1")
s_lucky = db_idx_set("is_lucky=1")
s_bb = db_idx_set("is_best_buddy=1")
s_mega = db_idx_set("is_mega_evolved=1")
s_powered = db_idx_set("is_powered_up=1")
s_purified = db_idx_set("is_purified_flag=1")

print(f"  hatched={len(s_hatched)}  traded={len(s_traded)}  lucky={len(s_lucky)}  bb={len(s_bb)}  mega={len(s_mega)}")

# Pull DB scalars for matching
db_pokemon = {}  # idx -> dict
rows = c.execute("""SELECT uid, species_name, level, cp, traded_time_ms, creation_time_ms,
    weather_boosted, num_additional_cpm, alignment, original_owner, costume, form, original_location_hash,
    is_powered_up, num_upgrades_or_battles, num_poweredup_or_walks, buddy_km_walked, mega_cpm,
    is_mega_evolved, mega_evo_state
    FROM pokemon""").fetchall()
for row in rows:
    uid_signed = row[0]
    u = signed_to_unsigned(uid_signed)
    idx = uid_to_idx.get(u)
    if idx is None: continue
    db_pokemon[idx] = {
        'uid': uid_signed,
        'name': row[1], 'lvl': row[2], 'cp': row[3], 'traded_ms': row[4], 'creation_ms': row[5],
        'weather': row[6], 'num_addl_cpm': row[7], 'align': row[8], 'orig_owner': row[9],
        'costume': row[10], 'form': row[11], 'orig_loc_hash': row[12],
        'powered': row[13], 'upg': row[14], 'walks': row[15], 'buddy_km': row[16], 'mcpm': row[17],
        'mega': row[18], 'mstate': row[19],
    }

print()
print("=" * 100)
print("ALIGNED 4-BYTE OFFSETS - FULL STATS")
print("=" * 100)
print(f"{'Off':>4} {'NZ':>5} {'Dist':>5} {'Min':>10} {'Max':>10}  TopVals")

ALREADY_MAPPED = {32, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60, 92, 104, 108, 112, 116, 120, 124, 128, 136, 144, 160, 168, 172,
                  196, 200, 225, 248, 264, 272, 276, 296, 336, 340, 344, 348, 352, 440, 480, 496}
KNOWN_STR_PTR = {64, 184, 256, 304, 360, 384}

aligned_results = {}
for off in range(0, 509, 4):
    if off in ALREADY_MAPPED: continue
    in_strptr = any(off >= sp and off < sp + 8 for sp in KNOWN_STR_PTR)
    in_known_i64_upper = any(off == k + 4 for k in {32, 136, 160, 248, 264})

    ivals = [struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes if off+4<=len(bs)]
    fvals = [struct.unpack_from('<f', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes if off+4<=len(bs)]

    nz = sum(1 for v in ivals if v != 0)
    dist = len(set(ivals))

    # Float plausibility: positive finite, not NaN, in [0, 100000]
    f_pos = sum(1 for v in fvals if v == v and 0.0001 < v < 100000 and not math.isinf(v))

    # Top integer values
    top = Counter(v for v in ivals if v != 0).most_common(5)

    # Range
    nz_ivals = [v for v in ivals if v != 0]
    imin = min(nz_ivals) if nz_ivals else 0
    imax = max(nz_ivals) if nz_ivals else 0

    flag_marker = ''
    if in_strptr: flag_marker += '(str)'
    if in_known_i64_upper: flag_marker += '(i64hi)'

    aligned_results[off] = {
        'ivals': ivals, 'fvals': fvals,
        'nz': nz, 'dist': dist, 'top': top,
        'imin': imin, 'imax': imax,
        'f_pos': f_pos, 'flag': flag_marker,
    }

    if nz == 0:
        print(f"{off:>4}: ALL ZERO  {flag_marker}")
    else:
        topstr = ' '.join(f'{v}={c}' for v, c in top[:3])
        print(f"{off:>4}: nz={nz:>5} dist={dist:>5} range=[{imin},{imax}]  fpos={f_pos:>5}  top={topstr}  {flag_marker}")

# Now look at specific aligned candidates that might be hatch_distance, friendship_score, mega_expiry
print()
print("=" * 100)
print("HATCH DISTANCE candidate search")
print("=" * 100)

# Find offsets where the 377 hatched pokemon have nonzero values
# kmDistanceToHatch should be 2.0/5.0/7.0/10.0/12.0 km targets
for off in sorted(aligned_results.keys()):
    if off + 4 > 512: continue
    fvals = aligned_results[off]['fvals']
    nz_in_hatched = sum(1 for i in s_hatched if fvals[i] == fvals[i] and 0.5 < fvals[i] < 13)
    if nz_in_hatched > 100:
        # what values?
        v_counter = Counter(round(fvals[i], 2) for i in s_hatched if fvals[i] == fvals[i] and 0.5 < fvals[i] < 13)
        # check non-hatched have 0 or out-of-range values
        nz_in_non_hatched = sum(1 for i in range(N) if i not in s_hatched and fvals[i] == fvals[i] and 0.5 < fvals[i] < 13)
        print(f"  off={off:>3}  hatched_in_range={nz_in_hatched}/377  non_hatched_in_range={nz_in_non_hatched}  top: {v_counter.most_common(8)}")

# friendship buddy levels: 0-700K xp, but score (0/1/2/3/4) is 0=stranger 1=good 2=great 3=ultra 4=best

for off in range(0, 509, 4):

            for ts in ts_samples:

                    dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(ts/1000, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat()

    s = p.get('strings') or {}
    for k in s:
```

`pogo_extract/v2_correlate.py`:

```py
"""
Cross-correlate offset values with known DB columns.

Strategy: for each candidate offset (boolean or i32), build the set of UIDs
that have value=X. Compare with DB sets like is_traded, is_lucky, is_hatched, etc.

Score each pair by Jaccard similarity. Print best matches.
"""
import json, struct, pickle, sqlite3
from collections import Counter

with open('v2_scan_results.pkl', 'rb') as f:
    payload = pickle.load(f)
results = payload['results']
all_uids = payload['uids']  # uint64
N = payload['N']

print(f"Loaded {N} pokemon, {len(results)} offsets")

# Build map uid (uint64) -> index
uid_to_idx = {}
for i, u in enumerate(all_uids):
    uid_to_idx[u] = i

# Build maps from DB
conn = sqlite3.connect('pokemon.db')
c = conn.cursor()

# DB stores uid as signed int64. Convert to unsigned for matching.
def signed_to_unsigned(v):
    return v if v >= 0 else v + (1 << 64)

DB_FLAGS = ['is_lucky', 'is_traded', 'is_shiny', 'is_best_buddy',
            'is_hatched_from_egg', 'is_purified_flag', 'is_mega_evolved',
            'is_powered_up']

flag_sets = {}  # flagname -> set of indices in our all_bytes array
for flag in DB_FLAGS:
    rows = c.execute(f"SELECT uid FROM pokemon WHERE {flag}=1").fetchall()
    s = set()
    for (uid_signed,) in rows:
        uid_unsigned = signed_to_unsigned(uid_signed)
        if uid_unsigned in uid_to_idx:
            s.add(uid_to_idx[uid_unsigned])
    flag_sets[flag] = s
    print(f"  flag '{flag}': {len(s)}/{len(rows)} matched into proto array")

# Also extract continuous DB columns we want to correlate floats against
db_floats = {}  # colname -> list of (idx, value) where value is non-null/non-zero
for col in ['buddy_km_walked', 'mega_cpm', 'mega_cp', 'level', 'cp']:
    rows = c.execute(f"SELECT uid, {col} FROM pokemon WHERE {col} IS NOT NULL").fetchall()
    arr = []
    for uid_signed, val in rows:
        uid_unsigned = signed_to_unsigned(uid_signed)
        idx = uid_to_idx.get(uid_unsigned)
        if idx is not None:
            arr.append((idx, val))
    db_floats[col] = arr
    print(f"  col '{col}': {len(arr)} loaded")

# 1) Boolean correlations
print()
print("=" * 110)
print("BOOLEAN OFFSET vs DB FLAG correlations (Jaccard similarity, only top hits):")
print("=" * 110)
```

`pogo_extract/v2_final.py`:

```py
"""
Final pass: gather all the offsets we've identified and finalize hypotheses.

Also:
1. Look at the bytes adjacent to byte=1 fields to identify multi-byte field structures.
2. Investigate offset 268 more (pulled out earlier - "411=49, 404=42" as upper of int64 traded_time_ms)
3. Look at 280, 288 which were "all distinct" upper-bytes - could be timestamps for events
4. Check 220 - has 5412 nz with byte values 114-118 (looks like part of pointer)
5. Check 252 i32 vs known hash and confirm as 'tradingOriginalOwnerHash_'
"""
import json, struct, sqlite3
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timezone

POGO_LAUNCH_MS = 1467590400000
NOW_MS = int(datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000)

data = json.load(open('pokemon_v3.json'))
all_bytes = []
for p in data:
    raw = p.get('raw_proto', '')
    if len(raw) >= 1024:
        all_bytes.append(bytes.fromhex(raw))
N = len(all_bytes)

c = sqlite3.connect('pokemon.db').cursor()
def s2u(v): return v if v >= 0 else v + (1 << 64)
uid_to_idx = {}
for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes):
    uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
    uid_to_idx[uid] = i

# Check whether the 248-252 packing matches the original_location_hash hex stored in DB
print("=" * 100)
print("VALIDATE original_location_hash from i32@252 + i32@248 packing")
print("=" * 100)
mismatches = 0
matches = 0
for (uid_signed, hash_hex) in c.execute("SELECT uid, original_location_hash FROM pokemon WHERE is_traded=1 LIMIT 30"):
    u = s2u(uid_signed)
    idx = uid_to_idx.get(u)
    if idx is None: continue
    bs = all_bytes[idx]
    i32_252 = struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 252)[0] & 0xFFFFFFFF
    i32_248 = struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 248)[0] & 0xFFFFFFFF
    # Format as hex64
    expected = f"{i32_252:08x}{i32_248:08x}"
    # The DB stores it as signed -> may be negative ints. Just compare numeric.
    # The hash_hex is signed-int64 in hex (e.g. -663fbe9ec16b645e)
    actual_int = int(hash_hex, 16) if hash_hex.startswith('-') else int(hash_hex, 16)
    if hash_hex.startswith('-'):
        actual_int = -int(hash_hex[1:], 16)
    # Convert to unsigned 64
    if actual_int < 0:
        actual_int += 1 << 64
    actual_hex = f"{actual_int:016x}"
    if expected == actual_hex:
        matches += 1
    else:
        if mismatches < 3:
            print(f"  MISMATCH: db={hash_hex} (={actual_hex}) vs constructed={expected}")
        mismatches += 1
print(f"  matches={matches} mismatches={mismatches}")

# Now: look at offset 248 vs 252 more carefully
# i32@248 looks like float (0.5974, 0.297, etc.)
```

`pogo_extract/v2_lists.py`:

```py
"""
Look for list/repeated proto fields.
- pokemonTagIds_ would be a repeated int64 - typically encoded as a pointer to a contiguous buffer.
- buddyWalkedMegaEnergyAwards_ - same.
- moves_attached - same.

In a 512-byte struct backing a proto, repeated fields often appear as:
  +N+0 = pointer (8 bytes) to repeating buffer (or address-like int)
  +N+8 = count int32

Look at all 8-byte aligned spots where:
  - upper 32 bits look like a pointer (large int with structured pattern)
  - lower 32 bits + 8 bytes ahead is a small count
"""
import json, struct, sqlite3
from collections import Counter

data = json.load(open('pokemon_v3.json'))
all_bytes = []
for p in data:
    raw = p.get('raw_proto', '')
    if len(raw) >= 1024:
        all_bytes.append(bytes.fromhex(raw))
N = len(all_bytes)

# For each 8-byte slot, count how often the i64 is in "address space" range
# x86-64 small object pointers typically aren't great clue, but in C# the IL2CPP arrays would have pointers
# We can also look for repeated pattern: per-pokemon i64 changes (per-instance address)

# Field counts to find:
# moves_attached array - if only 2 distinct values across 5413 = NOT a list
# Tag IDs - 0..K integers between 1-1000

# Look for offsets where the value is a count: small int 0-10
print("=" * 100)
print("LIST COUNT CANDIDATES (i32 with values 0-20)")
print("=" * 100)
for off in range(0, 509, 4):
    if off + 4 > 512: continue
    vals = [struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes]
    in_range = sum(1 for v in vals if 0 <= v <= 20)
    nz = sum(1 for v in vals if 0 < v <= 20)
    if nz > 100 and in_range > 5400:
        # Distribution
        c_top = Counter(v for v in vals if 0 < v <= 20).most_common(8)
        # Skip if same value dominates 90%+ (it's a single field, not a count)
        first_count = c_top[0][1] if c_top else 0
        # If the values look discrete and small
        print(f"  off={off}: nz={nz} in[0,20]={in_range}  top={c_top}")

print()
print("=" * 100)
print("addedFriendshipScore_ search - look for INT or float, a small number, present mostly on TRADED pokemon")
print("=" * 100)

# For each 4-byte aligned offset, check if traded pokemon have nonzero values that small ones don't
conn = sqlite3.connect('pokemon.db')
c = conn.cursor()
def s2u(v): return v if v >= 0 else v + (1 << 64)

uid_to_idx = {}
for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes):
    uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
    uid_to_idx[uid] = i

s_traded = set()
for (uid_signed,) in c.execute("SELECT uid FROM pokemon WHERE is_traded=1"):
    u = s2u(uid_signed)
    if u in uid_to_idx:
        s_traded.add(uid_to_idx[u])

# Look for offsets where most/all of s_traded have a value, and most non-traded don't
for off in range(0, 509, 4):
    if off + 4 > 512: continue
    vals_i = [struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes]
    vals_f = [struct.unpack_from('<f', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes]

    # i32 in range 0-100
    nz_traded_low = sum(1 for i in s_traded if 0 < vals_i[i] <= 100)
    nz_non_traded_low = sum(1 for i in range(N) if i not in s_traded and 0 < vals_i[i] <= 100)
    if nz_traded_low > 50 and nz_traded_low > nz_non_traded_low * 5 + 20:
        c_top = Counter(vals_i[i] for i in s_traded if vals_i[i] != 0).most_common(8)
        print(f"  off={off}: i32 traded_in[1,100]={nz_traded_low}/{len(s_traded)}  non_traded={nz_non_traded_low}  top={c_top}")

    # f32 in range 0-200
    nz_traded_f = sum(1 for i in s_traded if 0.001 < vals_f[i] < 200)
    nz_non_traded_f = sum(1 for i in range(N) if i not in s_traded and 0.001 < vals_f[i] < 200)
    if nz_traded_f > 50 and nz_traded_f > nz_non_traded_f * 5 + 20:
        samples = [round(vals_f[i], 4) for i in list(s_traded)[:5] if vals_f[i] > 0]
        print(f"  off={off}: f32 traded_in[0,200]={nz_traded_f}/{len(s_traded)}  non_traded={nz_non_traded_f}  samples={samples}")

print()
print("=" * 100)
print("Looking at ALL offsets that are nonzero on traded pokemon: i32, range 1-1000")
print("=" * 100)

for off in range(0, 509, 4):
    if off + 4 > 512: continue
    vals = [struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes]
    nz_in_traded = sum(1 for i in s_traded if vals[i] != 0)
    if nz_in_traded >= 100:
        # Check if also nz in non-traded
        nz_total = sum(1 for v in vals if v != 0)
        if nz_in_traded > nz_total * 0.8:
            c_top = Counter(vals[i] for i in s_traded if vals[i] != 0).most_common(5)
            print(f"  off={off}: traded_nz={nz_in_traded}/120, total_nz={nz_total}  top={c_top}")

# Look at the 192 question more carefully - what do those 180 non-hatched have in common?
print()
print("=" * 100)
print("OFFSET 192 = 1 BUT NOT HATCHED - what other byte/i32 also = 1?")
print("=" * 100)

idx_192_not_hatched = set()
for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes):
    if 192 < len(bs) and bs[192] == 1:
        # Get UID
        uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
        # Check DB if hatched
        uid_signed = uid if uid < 2**63 else uid - 2**64
        row = c.execute("SELECT is_hatched_from_egg FROM pokemon WHERE uid=?", (uid_signed,)).fetchone()
        if row and row[0] == 0:
            idx_192_not_hatched.add(i)

print(f"Pokemon with 192=1 but NOT hatched: {len(idx_192_not_hatched)}")

# At each other byte offset, check if ALL of these have byte=1 (subset signal)
for off in range(0, 509):
    bvals = [bs[off] for bs in all_bytes if off < len(bs)]
    eq1_in_subset = sum(1 for i in idx_192_not_hatched if bvals[i] == 1)
    eq1_total = sum(1 for v in bvals if v == 1)
    if eq1_in_subset >= 80 and eq1_in_subset > eq1_total * 0.4:
        print(f"  off={off}: subset eq1={eq1_in_subset}/{len(idx_192_not_hatched)}  total eq1={eq1_total}")

# Maybe these are ALL caught with curveball/excellent throw?
# Check if any consistent 4-byte aligned i32 distinguishes them
print()
print("Looking for any consistent value at any offset for the 180 'special non-hatched' subset:")
for off in range(0, 509, 1):
    bvals = [bs[off] for bs in all_bytes if off < len(bs)]
    # Most common in subset
    c_subset = Counter(bvals[i] for i in idx_192_not_hatched).most_common(3)
    # Check if subset has unusually high count of one byte vs rest
    if c_subset and c_subset[0][1] > 150:  # at least 80% of subset
        v0, ct = c_subset[0]
        # Check count outside subset
        outside_count = sum(1 for i in range(N) if i not in idx_192_not_hatched and bvals[i] == v0)
        # If ratio inside-subset is much higher than outside
        in_pct = ct / len(idx_192_not_hatched)
        out_pct = outside_count / (N - len(idx_192_not_hatched))
        if in_pct > out_pct * 2 and v0 != 0:
            print(f"  off={off}: subset top byte = {v0} ({ct}/{len(idx_192_not_hatched)} = {in_pct*100:.0f}%) vs outside {out_pct*100:.0f}%")

conn.close()
```

```py
"""
More targeted investigation:
- 192: investigate Jigglypuff outlier; could be is_event_pokemon
- 277: 79 BB but only 13% - what subset specifically?
- 424: rarity / pokemon class enum
- Look at offsets 320-336 (4 bytes nz) - maybe rare flag or buddy adventure data
- Look at 412-440 (mega energy?)
"""
import json, struct, sqlite3

from datetime import datetime, timezone

POGO_LAUNCH_MS = 1467590400000
NOW_MS = int(datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000)

data = json.load(open('pokemon_v3.json'))
all_bytes = []
for p in data:
    raw = p.get('raw_proto', '')
    if len(raw) >= 1024:
        all_bytes.append(bytes.fromhex(raw))
N = len(all_bytes)

c = sqlite3.connect('pokemon.db').cursor()
def s2u(v): return v if v >= 0 else v + (1 << 64)
uid_to_idx = {}
for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes):
    uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
    uid_to_idx[uid] = i

def db_set(where):
    s = set()
    for (uid_signed,) in c.execute(f"SELECT uid FROM pokemon WHERE {where}").fetchall():
        u = s2u(uid_signed)
        if u in uid_to_idx:
            s.add(uid_to_idx[u])
    return s

s_hatched = db_set("is_hatched_from_egg=1")
s_traded = db_set("is_traded=1")
s_lucky = db_set("is_lucky=1")
s_bb = db_set("is_best_buddy=1")
s_mega = db_set("is_mega_evolved=1")
s_powered = db_set("is_powered_up=1")
s_purified = db_set("is_purified_flag=1")
s_shiny = db_set("is_shiny=1")

    weather_boosted, num_additional_cpm, alignment, costume, form, original_owner,

    is_mega_evolved, mega_evo_state, mega_cp, origin_detail, pokeball, gender, pokemon_id,
    is_legendary, is_mythical, can_mega_evolve

    if idx is None: continue
    db_full[idx] = r

# Investigate 277

print(f"  num_upgrades values in BB-but-not-277: top {Counter(ub_not_277).most_common(5)}")

km_in_277 = [db_full[i][15] for i in idx_277 if i in db_full]

nz_km_in = sum(1 for v in km_in_277 if v and v > 0)

print(f"  buddy_km > 0 in 277=1 set: {nz_km_in}/{len(km_in_277)}")

counts_by = Counter()
for idx in idx_277:
    if idx not in db_full: continue
    r = db_full[idx]
    counts_by[r[1]] += 1
```

```py
"""
Final sweeping pass:
- Look at every aligned offset 0-508 (skipping known) and label them with hypothesis
- Find sub-message offsets with structure (e.g. mega substruct 336-352, capture details 264-296)
"""
import json, struct, sqlite3
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timezone

POGO_LAUNCH_MS = 1467590400000

data = json.load(open('pokemon_v3.json'))
all_bytes = []
for p in data:
    raw = p.get('raw_proto', '')
    if len(raw) >= 1024:
        all_bytes.append(bytes.fromhex(raw))
N = len(all_bytes)

c = sqlite3.connect('pokemon.db').cursor()
def s2u(v): return v if v >= 0 else v + (1 << 64)
uid_to_idx = {}
for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes):
    uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
    uid_to_idx[uid] = i

# Build common subsets
def db_set(where):
    s = set()
    for (uid_signed,) in c.execute(f"SELECT uid FROM pokemon WHERE {where}").fetchall():
        u = s2u(uid_signed)
        if u in uid_to_idx:
            s.add(uid_to_idx[u])
    return s

# Things to check at 277:
# Maybe 277 = "has gym defender record"?
# 79 BB pokemon - those that have been deployed at gym for >= 1 hour?
# Niantic stores days_at_gym/total_battles_at_gym

# I wonder if 277 is something like 'has a buddy adventure event' — let's check it carefully
# Note bytes around 277 layout:
# 270 = 0
# 272 (already mapped: is_lucky)
# 276 = 0 (special_bg_id mapped here but stored as a separate i32)
# 277 = byte=1 for 82
# 278-279 = arbitrary i16 (e.g. 0x4f, 0x2b, 0x77, 0x30)
# 280-287 = i64 with values like c061c356740000 = pointer to managed object

# So 277 is byte 1 of a 4-byte field at 276
# Field at 276 = (byte276) (byte277=01) (byte278) (byte279)
# Where 276 was 'special_bg_id' i32. Re-read the stat: 276 nz=248 dist=109 range[0,493]
# Actually our existing reading of i32@276 got values like 70, 246, 103 - those are the LOWER byte!
# Wait, 'i32 little-endian' means LSB first. So i32@276 reads bytes 276,277,278,279.
# If byte 276=70 and byte 277=01 and others are 0, then i32 = 0x00000146 = 326.
# But the top says i32@276 nz=248 dist=109 range[0,493], top values 70=8, 246=7, 103=6
# So byte 276 is the low byte. 277=1 means high bit pattern 0x100.
# i32@276 = byte276 + (byte277<<8) + (byte278<<16) + (byte279<<24)

# Re-read 82 'byte277=1' pokemon's i32@276
print("Re-reading offset 276 i32 for the 82 pokemon with byte277=1:")
idx_277 = set(i for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes) if 277 < len(bs) and bs[277] == 1)
i32_276_vals = []
for idx in idx_277:
    bs = all_bytes[idx]
    v = struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 276)[0]
    i32_276_vals.append(v)
print(f"  {len(i32_276_vals)} values at i32@276 for 277=1 set; top: {Counter(i32_276_vals).most_common(10)}")

# Same for 277=0 set:
print()
print("i32@276 for byte277=0 pokemon:")
i32_276_zeros = [struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 276)[0] for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes) if not (277 < len(bs) and bs[277] == 1)]
print(f"  count={len(i32_276_zeros)} top={Counter(i32_276_zeros).most_common(10)}")

# Hmm, i32@276 for byte277=1 set should have value >= 256. Confirm.
# These look like 326, 343, 374, 304, etc. = i32 in 256-500 range
# The top values for byte277=0 are 70, 246, 103 = i32 < 256

# So i32@276 is REALLY the same field. byte277=1 just indicates value >= 256.
# So "offset 277=1" is actually "offset 276 (i32) has value >= 256".
# Which means it's the SAME field, not a new one. The OLD mapping at 276 to 'special_bg_id' may be incomplete.

# let me check all i32@276 distribution
print()
all_276 = [struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 276)[0] for bs in all_bytes]

print(f"  DB bg: {db_bg}")

# So 276 = special_bg_id is correct. The 'byte277' stats were just bytes from i32@276 values >= 256.
# Wait but the original mapping says 276 = 'is_powered_up' (no, that's a derived flag at num_additional_cpm)
# Looking at proto_offsets_discovered.md, offset 276 is in already-mapped set.

# DB column special_bg_id has values like 70, 246, 103 (small) but i32@276 has larger values.

    u = s2u(uid_s)
    idx = uid_to_idx.get(u)
    if idx is None: continue
    db_pos[idx] = (lat, lon)

print(f"  pokemon with lat/lon: {len(db_pos)}")
# For each f64 offset, check correlation with lat
import math
for off in range(0, 504, 4):
    if off + 8 > 512: continue
    matches = 0
    for idx, (lat, lon) in db_pos.items():
        bs = all_bytes[idx]
        try:
            f64 = struct.unpack_from('<d', bs, off)[0]
            if f64 == f64 and abs(f64 - lat) < 0.0001:
                matches += 1
        except: pass
    if matches > 5:
        print(f"  off={off} (f64): {matches}/{len(db_pos)} match LAT")

# Try f32 too
for off in range(0, 508, 4):
    if off + 4 > 512: continue
    matches = 0
    for idx, (lat, lon) in db_pos.items():
        bs = all_bytes[idx]
        try:
            f32 = struct.unpack_from('<f', bs, off)[0]
            if f32 == f32 and abs(f32 - lat) < 0.001:
                matches += 1
        except: pass
    if matches > 5:
        print(f"  off={off} (f32): {matches}/{len(db_pos)} match LAT")

# Look at offset 8 area which I haven't examined
print()
```

`pogo_extract/v2_scan.py`:

```py
"""
Comprehensive offset scan v2 - exhaustive byte-level statistics.

For every offset 0-508 not in known set, compute stats at multiple interpretations:
  - 1 byte (count of value=1, of nonzero)
  - 4-byte i32
  - 4-byte f32
  - 8-byte i64
  - 8-byte f64

Output CSV + a summary report.
"""
import json, struct, math
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timezone

POGO_LAUNCH_MS = 1467590400000
NOW_MS = int(datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000)

# Already mapped (4-byte aligned positions known to hold field data)
ALREADY_MAPPED = {32, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60, 92, 104, 108, 112, 116, 120, 124, 128,
                  136, 144, 160, 168, 172, 196, 200, 225, 248, 264, 272, 276, 296,
                  336, 340, 344, 348, 352, 440, 480, 496}
# String-ptr 8-byte offsets known
KNOWN_STR_PTR = {64, 184, 256, 304, 360, 384}

print("Loading pokemon_v3.json...")
data = json.load(open('pokemon_v3.json'))
print(f"  {len(data)} pokemon")

all_bytes = []
all_uids = []
for p in data:
    raw = p.get('raw_proto', '')
    if len(raw) >= 1024:
        all_bytes.append(bytes.fromhex(raw))
        try:
            uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', all_bytes[-1], 32)[0]
            all_uids.append(uid)
        except:
            all_uids.append(0)

N = len(all_bytes)
print(f"  {N} have 512+ byte protos\n")

# Build per-offset results dict
results = []  # list of dicts

for off in range(0, 509):
    rec = {'off': off}

    # 1-byte view
    bvals = [bs[off] for bs in all_bytes if off < len(bs)]
    bnz = sum(1 for v in bvals if v != 0)
    bones = sum(1 for v in bvals if v == 1)
    btwos = sum(1 for v in bvals if v == 2)
    rec['b_nz'] = bnz
    rec['b_eq1'] = bones
    rec['b_eq2'] = btwos
    rec['b_distinct'] = len(set(bvals))
    rec['b_top'] = Counter(bvals).most_common(5)

    # 4-byte i32
    if off + 4 <= 512:
        ivals = [struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes if off + 4 <= len(bs)]
        i_nz = sum(1 for v in ivals if v != 0)
        i_distinct = len(set(ivals))
        i_min = min(ivals) if ivals else 0
        i_max = max(ivals) if ivals else 0
        rec['i_nz'] = i_nz
        rec['i_distinct'] = i_distinct
        rec['i_min'] = i_min
        rec['i_max'] = i_max
        rec['i_top'] = Counter(v for v in ivals if v != 0).most_common(5)
        rec['i_vals'] = ivals  # for cross-correlation later

        # 4-byte f32
        fvals = [struct.unpack_from('<f', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes if off + 4 <= len(bs)]
        f_pos_finite = sum(1 for v in fvals if v == v and 0.0001 < v < 1e6 and not math.isinf(v))
        f_neg_finite = sum(1 for v in fvals if v == v and -1e6 < v < -0.0001 and not math.isinf(v))
        f_in_001_5 = sum(1 for v in fvals if v == v and 0.0001 < v < 5)  # CPMs / friendship norm
        f_in_5_100 = sum(1 for v in fvals if v == v and 5 <= v < 100)   # km / friendship score
        f_in_100_5000 = sum(1 for v in fvals if v == v and 100 <= v < 5000)
        rec['f_pos'] = f_pos_finite
        rec['f_neg'] = f_neg_finite
        rec['f_001_5'] = f_in_001_5
        rec['f_5_100'] = f_in_5_100
        rec['f_100_5000'] = f_in_100_5000
        rec['f_vals'] = fvals
    else:
        rec.update({'i_nz': 0, 'i_distinct': 0, 'i_min': 0, 'i_max': 0, 'i_top': [], 'i_vals': [],
                    'f_pos': 0, 'f_neg': 0, 'f_001_5': 0, 'f_5_100': 0, 'f_100_5000': 0, 'f_vals': []})

    # 8-byte i64 (timestamp candidate)
    if off + 8 <= 512:
        qvals = [struct.unpack_from('<q', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes if off + 8 <= len(bs)]
        q_ts_count = sum(1 for v in qvals if POGO_LAUNCH_MS < v < NOW_MS + 86400000)
        q_nz = sum(1 for v in qvals if v != 0)
        q_distinct = len(set(qvals))
        rec['q_nz'] = q_nz
        rec['q_distinct'] = q_distinct
        rec['q_ts_count'] = q_ts_count
        rec['q_top'] = Counter(v for v in qvals if v != 0).most_common(5)
        rec['q_vals'] = qvals
    else:
        rec.update({'q_nz': 0, 'q_distinct': 0, 'q_ts_count': 0, 'q_top': [], 'q_vals': []})

    results.append(rec)

# Save the raw results to a pickle for downstream use
import pickle
pickle.dump({'results': results, 'uids': all_uids, 'N': N}, open('v2_scan_results.pkl', 'wb'))

# ============================
# Print summary tables
# ============================

# 1) Offsets with notable boolean signal (rare 1-byte=1)
print("=" * 110)
print("BOOLEAN-LIKE OFFSETS (1-byte values, where eq1 count is 5..1500 and dominant byte=0 or 1):")
print("=" * 110)
print(f"{'Off':>4} {'eq1':>5} {'eq2':>5} {'NZ':>5} {'Dist':>5} {'AlreadyMapped':>13}  TopBytes")
for r in results:
    off = r['off']
    if 5 <= r['b_eq1'] <= 1500 and r['b_distinct'] <= 6 and r['b_eq1'] >= r['b_eq2']:
        m = '*' if off in ALREADY_MAPPED else ''
        in_strptr = any(off >= sp and off < sp + 8 for sp in KNOWN_STR_PTR)
        m += ' (str)' if in_strptr else ''
        print(f"{off:>4} {r['b_eq1']:>5} {r['b_eq2']:>5} {r['b_nz']:>5} {r['b_distinct']:>5} {m:>13}  {r['b_top']}")

# 2) Offsets with notable i32 signal (nz between 5 and 4000, distinct > 5)
print()
print("=" * 110)
print("I32 OFFSETS (nz=5..5000, distinct>=5; potential counters/IDs):")
print("=" * 110)
print(f"{'Off':>4} {'NZ':>5} {'Dist':>5} {'Min':>11} {'Max':>11} {'Marked':>8}  TopVals")
for r in results:
    off = r['off']
    if r['i_nz'] >= 5 and r['i_distinct'] >= 5 and r['i_nz'] <= 5000:
        # exclude if value range looks like garbage 32-bit pointer (huge min/max)
        if r['i_min'] < -1e9 or r['i_max'] > 1e9:
            continue
        m = '*' if off in ALREADY_MAPPED else ''
        in_strptr = any(off >= sp and off < sp + 8 for sp in KNOWN_STR_PTR)
        m += '(str)' if in_strptr else ''
        # also not aligned to 4? note it
        if off % 4 != 0: m += '!unalign'
        top3 = r['i_top'][:3]
        print(f"{off:>4} {r['i_nz']:>5} {r['i_distinct']:>5} {r['i_min']:>11} {r['i_max']:>11} {m:>8}  {top3}")

# 3) Float candidates (positive finite count interesting)
print()
print("=" * 110)
print("F32 OFFSETS (where many values are positive finite reals):")
print("=" * 110)
print(f"{'Off':>4} {'fPos':>5} {'in0-5':>6} {'in5-100':>7} {'in100-5k':>8} {'iNZ':>5} {'Marked':>8}  Sample floats")
for r in results:
    off = r['off']
    if r['f_pos'] >= 30 and (r['f_001_5'] >= 30 or r['f_5_100'] >= 30 or r['f_100_5000'] >= 30):
        m = '*' if off in ALREADY_MAPPED else ''
        in_strptr = any(off >= sp and off < sp + 8 for sp in KNOWN_STR_PTR)
        m += '(str)' if in_strptr else ''
        if off % 4 != 0: m += '!unalign'
        # Get a few example floats
        samples = [round(v, 4) for v in r['f_vals'][:200] if v == v and 0.0001 < v < 1e6][:5]
        print(f"{off:>4} {r['f_pos']:>5} {r['f_001_5']:>6} {r['f_5_100']:>7} {r['f_100_5000']:>8} {r['i_nz']:>5} {m:>8}  {samples}")

# 4) Timestamp candidates
print()
print("=" * 110)
print("TIMESTAMP CANDIDATES (i64 in valid PoGo range, count>=10):")
print("=" * 110)
print(f"{'Off':>4} {'TSct':>5} {'NZ':>5} {'Dist':>5} {'Marked':>8}  Sample TS")
for r in results:
    off = r['off']
    if r['q_ts_count'] >= 10:
        m = '*' if off in ALREADY_MAPPED else ''
        in_strptr = any(off >= sp and off < sp + 8 for sp in KNOWN_STR_PTR)
        m += '(str)' if in_strptr else ''
        # one example TS
        ts_sample = next((v for v in r['q_vals'] if POGO_LAUNCH_MS < v < NOW_MS + 86400000), 0)
        try:
            dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(ts_sample/1000, tz=timezone.utc).isoformat() if ts_sample else '-'
        except:
            dt = '?'
        print(f"{off:>4} {r['q_ts_count']:>5} {r['q_nz']:>5} {r['q_distinct']:>5} {m:>8}  {ts_sample} ({dt})")

print()
print("Done. Saved v2_scan_results.pkl for downstream cross-correlation.")

```

`pogo_extract/v2_validate.py`:

```py
"""
Validate all candidate offsets and produce final examples.

Test all our hypotheses:
- 148 (i32 nz=23 1-18) = ???
- 176 (i32 nz=104 val=1) = ???
- 192 (byte=1 for 557) = ???
- 269 (byte=1 for 119/120 traded) = is_traded_flag
- 248 (f32) = addedFriendshipScore
- 252 (i32) = tradingOriginalOwnerHash
- 424 (i32) = pokemon_size_category
- 192 needs more investigation

Also: look for any leftover features in unmapped 4-byte offsets
"""
import json, struct, sqlite3
from collections import Counter

data = json.load(open('pokemon_v3.json'))
all_bytes = []
for p in data:
    raw = p.get('raw_proto', '')
    if len(raw) >= 1024:
        all_bytes.append(bytes.fromhex(raw))
N = len(all_bytes)

c = sqlite3.connect('pokemon.db').cursor()
def s2u(v): return v if v >= 0 else v + (1 << 64)
uid_to_idx = {}
for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes):
    uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
    uid_to_idx[uid] = i

def db_set(where):
    s = set()
    for (uid_signed,) in c.execute(f"SELECT uid FROM pokemon WHERE {where}").fetchall():
        u = s2u(uid_signed)
        if u in uid_to_idx:
            s.add(uid_to_idx[u])
    return s

s_traded = db_set("is_traded=1")
s_bb = db_set("is_best_buddy=1")
s_powered = db_set("is_powered_up=1")
s_purified = db_set("is_purified_flag=1")
s_mega = db_set("is_mega_evolved=1")
s_hatched = db_set("is_hatched_from_egg=1")

# ==========================================================================
print("=" * 100)
print("OFFSET 269 VALIDATION (hypothesized = is_traded)")
print("=" * 100)

idx_269 = set(i for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes) if 269 < len(bs) and bs[269] == 1)
overlap_traded = len(idx_269 & s_traded)
not_traded_269 = idx_269 - s_traded
traded_not_269 = s_traded - idx_269
print(f"269=1 set size: {len(idx_269)}")
print(f"Overlap with traded: {overlap_traded}/120")
print(f"269=1 but NOT traded: {len(not_traded_269)}")
print(f"Traded but 269=0: {len(traded_not_269)}")

# Show edge cases
if not_traded_269:
    for idx in list(not_traded_269)[:3]:
        bs = all_bytes[idx]
        uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
        uid_signed = uid if uid < 2**63 else uid - 2**64
        row = c.execute("SELECT species_name, original_owner, traded_time_ms FROM pokemon WHERE uid=?", (uid_signed,)).fetchone()
        print(f"  269=1 NOT traded: {row}")
if traded_not_269:
    for idx in list(traded_not_269)[:3]:
        bs = all_bytes[idx]
        uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
        uid_signed = uid if uid < 2**63 else uid - 2**64
        row = c.execute("SELECT species_name, original_owner, traded_time_ms FROM pokemon WHERE uid=?", (uid_signed,)).fetchone()
        print(f"  traded but 269=0: {row}")

# Confirmed 269 = is_traded_flag

# ==========================================================================
print()
print("=" * 100)
print("VALIDATE 248 = addedFriendshipScore (float bit-pattern of original_location_hash low half)")
print("=" * 100)

# Already validated. Specifically: f32@248 = friendship % added (0..0.7)
# Per-trader, the value varies per pokemon (varies 0 to 0.7)
print("Sample values per trader OyeBenny (44 pokemon):")
trades_to = []
for (uid_s, owner) in c.execute("SELECT uid, original_owner FROM pokemon WHERE original_owner='OyeBenny'").fetchall():
    u = s2u(uid_s)
    idx = uid_to_idx.get(u)
    if idx is None: continue
    bs = all_bytes[idx]
    f = struct.unpack_from('<f', bs, 248)[0]
    trades_to.append(f)
trades_to.sort()
print(f"  Sorted f@248 for OyeBenny: {[round(f, 4) for f in trades_to[::4]]}")  # every 4th

# These values range 0.0-0.7 - looks like cumulative friendship%

# ==========================================================================
print()
print("=" * 100)
print("VALIDATE 424 = pokemon_size_category (XS/S/N/L/XL/XXL)")
print("=" * 100)

# size 4 = heaviest avg. Confirm with actual game-known XL pokemon
# E.g. Gyarados has 6 with 424=1, 30 with 424=3
# Pumpkaboo: small/avg/large/super sizes (in PoGo) = 4 distinct values
pump_pump = list(c.execute("SELECT uid, weight_kg, height_m FROM pokemon WHERE species_name='Pumpkaboo' ORDER BY weight_kg"))
print(f"Pumpkaboo by weight (= small/avg/large/super-size form):")
for uid_s, w, h in pump_pump[:20]:
    u = s2u(uid_s)
    idx = uid_to_idx.get(u)
    if idx is None: continue
    bs = all_bytes[idx]
    v = struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 424)[0]
    print(f"  weight={w:.2f} height={h:.3f} 424={v}")

# Mostly Pumpkaboo small (lightest) = 424=2 or 3
# Pumpkaboo super-size (heaviest) = 424=5

# Try all-time XL/XXL pokemon (Slugma? Scizor?)
print()

print()
print("=" * 100)
print("OFFSET 268 - upper i32 of int64 traded_time_ms (already mapped)")
print("=" * 100)

# Already-mapped clarification: 264-271 are int64 traded_time_ms.

print("=" * 100)

    if row:

# = (hatched OR traded OR research OR raid OR research_breakthrough OR special_event)

    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE is_hatched_from_egg=1 OR is_traded=1
""").fetchone()[0]
print(f"DB hatched OR traded: {not_wild}")

print(f"  intersection with 192=1: {len(idx_192 & hatched_or_traded)}")
print(f"  192=1 but NOT (hatched OR traded): {len(idx_192 - hatched_or_traded)}")

# Theory abandoned. Mark as 'unknown distinctive field; possibly is_special_acquisition'

# Other candidates to check - i32 unaligned = part of larger field, but the BYTE @277 might be its own bool
# Let me check if there's any VALUE distinct to those 79 BB
# These BB pokemon all have move3 set. So 277=1 is just 'move3 ID >= 256'.
# Let's verify:
print()
print("=" * 100)
print("Confirm 277 = move3 high byte (NOT a new field)")
print("=" * 100)

idx_277 = set(i for i, bs in enumerate(all_bytes) if 277 < len(bs) and bs[277] == 1)
for idx in list(idx_277)[:5]:
    bs = all_bytes[idx]
    uid = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
    uid_signed = uid if uid < 2**63 else uid - 2**64
    move3 = struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 276)[0]
    row = c.execute("SELECT species_name, move1, move2 FROM pokemon WHERE uid=?", (uid_signed,)).fetchone()
    print(f"  move3={move3}: {row}")

# Yes - move3 IDs are 256-500 range for BB pokemon (newer moves like Aerial Ace = 333, etc.)

# ==========================================================================
# Final sweep - look for any aligned offset I missed
print()
print("=" * 100)
print("FINAL SWEEP - 4-byte aligned offsets with NZ count >= 50 not mapped")
print("=" * 100)

ALREADY_MAPPED = {32, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60, 92, 104, 108, 112, 116, 120, 124, 128, 136, 144, 160, 168, 172,
                  196, 200, 225, 248, 252, 264, 268, 272, 276, 296, 336, 340, 344, 348, 352, 424, 440, 480, 496}
KNOWN_STR_PTR = {64, 184, 256, 304, 360, 384}

candidates = []
for off in range(0, 509, 4):
    if off in ALREADY_MAPPED: continue
    if any(off >= sp and off < sp + 8 for sp in KNOWN_STR_PTR): continue
    if off + 4 > 512: continue
    ivals = [struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, off)[0] for bs in all_bytes]
    nz = sum(1 for v in ivals if v != 0)
    if nz >= 50:
        candidates.append((off, nz, len(set(ivals))))

print(f"  candidates with NZ >= 50:")
for off, nz, dist in candidates:
    print(f"    off={off}: nz={nz} dist={dist}")
```

`pogo_extract/validate.py`:

```py
"""
Triple-check: validate the pokemon database for false positives.

Tests:
1. Duplicate uid detection
2. Same species + same IVs + same level → same CP (sanity)
3. Impossible CP / level combos
4. IV distribution sanity (hundos shouldn't be 10%+)
5. Hundo cluster check: same species hundos at same level must have IDENTICAL CP
6. CPM should match a known game CPM value (within 0.0001)
7. Pokemon ID in valid range (1-1025)
8. Move IDs in reasonable range
9. Creation date sanity
10. Compare extraction count to expected
"""
import sqlite3, struct
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

KNOWN_CPMS = set()
CPM_LIST = [
    0.094,0.135137432,0.16639787,0.192650919,0.21573247,0.236572661,
    0.25572005,0.273530381,0.29024988,0.306057377,0.3210876,0.335445036,
    0.34921268,0.362457751,0.37523559,0.387592406,0.39956728,0.411193551,
    0.42250001,0.432926419,0.44310755,0.4530599578,0.46279839,0.472336083,
    0.48168495,0.4908558,0.49985844,0.508701765,0.51739395,0.525942511,
    0.53435433,0.542635767,0.55079269,0.558830576,0.56675452,0.574569153,
    0.58227891,0.589887907,0.59740001,0.604818814,0.61215729,0.619399365,
    0.62656713,0.633644533,0.64065295,0.647576426,0.65443563,0.661214806,
    0.667934,0.674577537,0.68116492,0.687680648,0.69414365,0.700538673,
    0.70688421,0.713164996,0.71939909,0.725571552,0.7317,0.734741009,
    0.73776948,0.740785574,0.74378943,0.746781211,0.74976104,0.752729087,
    0.75568551,0.758630378,0.76156384,0.764486065,0.76739717,0.770297266,
    0.7731865,0.776064962,0.77893275,0.781790055,0.78463697,0.787473578,
    0.79030001,0.792803968,0.79530001,0.797800015,0.8003,0.802799995,
    0.8053,0.807800015,0.81029999,0.812799985,0.81529999,0.81779999,
    0.82029999,0.82279999,0.82529999,0.82779999,0.83029999,0.83279999,
    0.83529999,0.83779999,0.84029999,0.84279999,0.84529999
]

def cpm_close(cpm):
    """True if CPM matches a known PoGo CPM within tolerance."""
    return any(abs(cpm - k) < 0.0001 for k in CPM_LIST)

conn = sqlite3.connect('pokemon.db')
c = conn.cursor()

print("=" * 70)
print("TRIPLE-CHECK VALIDATION")
print("=" * 70)

# 1. Duplicate UIDs
c.execute("SELECT uid_hex, COUNT(*) FROM pokemon GROUP BY uid_hex HAVING COUNT(*) > 1")
dups = c.fetchall()
print(f"\n1. Duplicate UIDs: {len(dups)} (should be 0)")
if dups:
    for d in dups[:5]: print(f"   {d}")

# 2. CPM sanity - all CPMs should match a known game value
c.execute("SELECT cp_multiplier FROM pokemon")
all_cpms = [r[0] for r in c.fetchall()]
bad_cpms = sum(1 for cpm in all_cpms if not cpm_close(cpm))
print(f"\n2. Pokemon with CPM not matching known PoGo values: {bad_cpms}/{len(all_cpms)}")

# 3. PokemonId range
c.execute("SELECT pokemon_id, COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE pokemon_id < 1 OR pokemon_id > 1025 GROUP BY pokemon_id")
oor = c.fetchall()
print(f"\n3. Pokemon ID out of range (1-1025): {len(oor)} unique IDs")
if oor:
    for r in oor[:10]: print(f"   #{r[0]}: {r[1]} entries")

# 4. Same species + IVs + level → same CP test
print(f"\n4. CP consistency check (same species/IVs/level should = same CP):")
c.execute("""SELECT pokemon_id, iv_atk, iv_def, iv_sta, ROUND(cp_multiplier, 5) cpm,
                    GROUP_CONCAT(cp), COUNT(*) cnt, COUNT(DISTINCT cp) distinct_cps
             FROM pokemon
             WHERE num_additional_cpm = 0
             GROUP BY pokemon_id, iv_atk, iv_def, iv_sta, cpm
             HAVING COUNT(*) > 1""")
groups = c.fetchall()
inconsistent = [g for g in groups if g[7] > 1]
print(f"   Groups with 2+ pokemon: {len(groups)}")
print(f"   Groups where CP differs: {len(inconsistent)} (should be 0 or near-zero)")
if inconsistent:
    print(f"   Sample inconsistent groups:")
    for g in inconsistent[:5]:
        print(f"     species={g[0]} ivs={g[1]}/{g[2]}/{g[3]} cpm={g[4]} CPs={g[5]}")

# 5. Hundo cluster CP test
print(f"\n5. Hundo CP consistency by species/level:")
c.execute("""SELECT pokemon_id, ROUND(cp_multiplier, 5) cpm,
                    GROUP_CONCAT(cp), COUNT(*) cnt, COUNT(DISTINCT cp) distinct_cps
             FROM pokemon WHERE is_hundo AND num_additional_cpm = 0
             GROUP BY pokemon_id, cpm
             HAVING COUNT(*) > 1""")
hundo_groups = c.fetchall()
bad_hundos = [g for g in hundo_groups if g[4] > 1]
print(f"   Hundo groups (same species + level): {len(hundo_groups)}")
print(f"   Groups with INCONSISTENT CP: {len(bad_hundos)}")
if bad_hundos:
    print(f"   These differing CPs indicate FALSE POSITIVES:")
    for g in bad_hundos[:5]:
        print(f"     species={g[0]} cpm={g[1]} CPs={g[2]}")

# 6. CP/CPM/IV math check (simplified)
print(f"\n6. CP/level sanity check:")
# A pokemon's CP = (atk*sqrt(def)*sqrt(sta)*cpm^2)/10 where atk,def,sta = base+iv
# Without base stats we can't verify exactly, but extreme cases:
# - CP > 5500 at level < 30 is impossible without best buddy
# - CP < 50 at level 30+ is impossible
suspicious = []
c.execute("""SELECT pokemon_id, species_name, cp, level, num_additional_cpm
             FROM pokemon
             WHERE (cp > 5500 AND level < 25 AND num_additional_cpm = 0)
                OR (cp < 30 AND level > 25)""")
for r in c.fetchall():
    suspicious.append(r)
print(f"   Suspicious CP/level combos: {len(suspicious)}")
for r in suspicious[:5]: print(f"     {r}")

# 7. Move ID range
c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE move1 < 0 OR move1 > 600")
print(f"\n7. Move1 out of range (0-600): {c.fetchone()[0]}")
c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE move2 < 0 OR move2 > 600")
print(f"   Move2 out of range: {c.fetchone()[0]}")

# 8. Date sanity
c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE creation_time_ms < 1467590400000")
print(f"\n8. Creation before PoGo launch (filter check): {c.fetchone()[0]} (should be 0)")
c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE creation_time_ms > 1800000000000")  # ~Jan 2027
print(f"   Creation after Jan 2027: {c.fetchone()[0]}")

# 9. Pokeball valid range
c.execute("SELECT pokeball, COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE pokeball NOT IN (0,1,2,3,4,5) GROUP BY pokeball")
bad_balls = c.fetchall()
print(f"\n9. Invalid pokeball values: {sum(b[1] for b in bad_balls)}")
for b in bad_balls[:5]: print(f"   pokeball={b[0]}: {b[1]}")

# 10. Best buddy check - num_additional_cpm should be > 0 for is_best_buddy
c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE is_best_buddy AND num_additional_cpm = 0")
print(f"\n10. Best Buddy with 0 boost (mismatch): {c.fetchone()[0]}")

# 11. Compare hundo rate
total = c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pokemon").fetchone()[0]
hundos = c.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE is_hundo").fetchone()[0]
print(f"\n11. Hundo rate: {hundos}/{total} = {hundos/total*100:.2f}%")
print(f"    (Real wild hundo rate ~0.024%; with weather ~0.066%; user has 10.4%)")
print(f"    HIGH but possible if user uses Pokemod spawning features.")

# 12. Per-species hundo concentration
print(f"\n12. Hundo distribution by species:")
c.execute("""SELECT species_name, COUNT(*) FROM pokemon WHERE is_hundo
             GROUP BY species_name ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5""")
for r in c.fetchall():
    print(f"    {r[0]}: {r[1]}")

# 13. Quick spot check on sample
print(f"\n13. Sample pokemon (random 5):")
c.execute("""SELECT species_name, cp, iv_atk, iv_def, iv_sta, level,
                    pokeball_name, gender_name, is_hundo, is_lucky, is_shiny, creation_date
             FROM pokemon ORDER BY RANDOM() LIMIT 5""")
for r in c.fetchall():
    print(f"    {r[0]} CP{r[1]} IV{r[2]}/{r[3]}/{r[4]} L{r[5]} {r[6]} {r[7]} hundo={r[8]} lucky={r[9]} shiny={r[10]} {r[11][:10] if r[11] else None}")

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("SUMMARY")
print("=" * 70)
flags = []
if len(dups) > 0: flags.append(f"{len(dups)} duplicate UIDs")
if bad_cpms > total * 0.01: flags.append(f"{bad_cpms} bad CPMs (potential false positives)")
if len(oor) > 0: flags.append(f"{sum(r[1] for r in oor)} pokemon with bad species ID")
if len(bad_hundos) > 0: flags.append(f"{len(bad_hundos)} inconsistent hundo CP groups (false positives)")
if len(suspicious) > 0: flags.append(f"{len(suspicious)} suspicious CP/level combos")

if not flags:
    print("PASS: All consistency checks passed.")
    print(f"5394 pokemon are internally consistent.")
else:
    print("ISSUES FOUND:")
    for f in flags: print(f"  - {f}")

conn.close()
```

`pogo_extract/verify_4hundo.py`:

```py
import sqlite3, os

DB = r"C:/Users/Blanco/Desktop/Claude Operations/Phone Maintenance/pogo_extract/pokemon.db"
TAGDIR = r"C:/Users/Blanco/Desktop/Claude Operations/Phone Maintenance/pogo_extract/system/analysis/tagsets"
HUNDO_FILE = os.path.join(TAGDIR, "4_Hundo.txt")
TRANSFER_FILE = os.path.join(TAGDIR, "6_Transfer.txt")

def load_uids(path):
    s = set()
    dups = 0
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        for line in f:
            u = line.strip()
            if not u:
                continue
            if u in s:
                dups += 1
            s.add(u)  # keep verbatim string, no int()/reformat
    return s, dups

conn = sqlite3.connect(DB)
cur = conn.cursor()

# Rule: in_bag=1 AND iv_total=45  (string uid_hex verbatim)
cur.execute("SELECT uid_hex FROM pokemon WHERE in_bag=1 AND iv_total=45")
rule_rows = [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
rule_set = set(rule_rows)
print("rule rows:", len(rule_rows), "distinct uid_hex:", len(rule_set))

# Sanity: confirm any uid_hex not 16 chars, or non-hex
bad = [u for u in rule_set if len(u) != 16]
print("rule uids with len!=16:", bad)

# Transfer set
transfer_set, t_dups = load_uids(TRANSFER_FILE)
print("transfer file uids:", len(transfer_set), "dups-in-file:", t_dups)

# Derived = rule - transfer (no keep tag may contain a transfer mon)
derived = rule_set - transfer_set
overlap = rule_set & transfer_set
print("rule ∩ transfer (removed):", len(overlap))
print("DERIVED count:", len(derived))

# File set
file_set, h_dups = load_uids(HUNDO_FILE)
print("hundo file uids:", len(file_set), "dups-in-file:", h_dups)

# Compare (direct string compare)
extra = file_set - derived      # in file, not derived
missing = derived - file_set    # derived, not in file
match = (len(extra) == 0 and len(missing) == 0)
print("EXTRA (file - derived):", len(extra))
print("MISSING (derived - file):", len(missing))
print("MATCH:", match)

# Does the file itself contain any transfer mon? (the rule the tagset must obey)
file_transfer_overlap = file_set & transfer_set
print("file ∩ transfer (violation):", len(file_transfer_overlap), sorted(file_transfer_overlap)[:8])

# context for discrepancies
def ctx(uids):
    out = []
    for u in sorted(uids)[:8]:
        cur.execute("SELECT uid_hex, species_name, iv_atk, iv_def, iv_sta, iv_total, in_bag, gl_rank, cull_decision_v9 FROM pokemon WHERE uid_hex=?", (u,))
        row = cur.fetchone()
        if row is None:
            out.append((u, "NOT-IN-DB"))
        else:
            out.append(row)
    return out

print("\n--- EXTRA context (in file, not derived) ---")
for r in ctx(extra):
    print(r)
print("\n--- MISSING context (derived, not in file) ---")
for r in ctx(missing):
    print(r)

conn.close()
```

```py
    "TP": [],  # TRANSFER with CLAUDE_TX (correct)
    "FP": [],  # KEEP with CLAUDE_TX (BAD - false positive)
    "FN": [],  # TRANSFER without CLAUDE_TX (coverage gap)
    "TN": [],  # KEEP without CLAUDE_TX (correct)
    "PROTO_NOT_FOUND": [],  # couldn't resolve to heap pointer
    "TAGS_NULL": [],  # GetAllTags returned null
}

t0 = time.time()
for i, (uid, uid_hex, sp, cp, iv, decision, is_h, is_l, is_s, is_b, alignment) in enumerate(rows):
    low = uid & 0xFFFFFFFF; high = (uid >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    if low > 0x7FFFFFFF: low -= 0x100000000
    if high > 0x7FFFFFFF: high -= 0x100000000
    p = script.exports_sync.find_pokemon_proto(low, high)
    if not p.get("ok"):
        results["PROTO_NOT_FOUND"].append((uid_hex, sp, cp, iv, decision))
        continue
    res = script.exports_sync.get_pokemon_tags(real, p["ptr"])
    if not res.get("ok"):
        results["TAGS_NULL"].append((uid_hex, sp, cp, iv, decision))
        continue
    tags = res.get("tags") or []
    has_tx = "CLAUDE_TX" in tags
    rec = (uid_hex, sp, cp, iv, decision, is_h, is_l, is_s, is_b, alignment, tags)
    if decision == "TRANSFER" and has_tx: results["TP"].append(rec)
    elif decision == "KEEP" and has_tx: results["FP"].append(rec)
    elif decision == "TRANSFER" and not has_tx: results["FN"].append(rec)
    else: results["TN"].append(rec)

    if (i+1) % 500 == 0:
        elapsed = time.time() - t0
        rate = (i+1)/elapsed
        eta = (len(rows)-i-1)/rate
        print(f"  {i+1}/{len(rows)} | TP={len(results['TP'])} FP={len(results['FP'])} FN={len(results['FN'])} TN={len(results['TN'])} not_found={len(results['PROTO_NOT_FOUND'])} | rate={rate:.0f}/s eta={eta:.0f}s")

print()
print("=" * 70)
print("FULL VERIFICATION RESULTS")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"  True Positive (TRANSFER + tagged):  {len(results['TP'])}")
print(f"  FALSE POSITIVE (KEEP + tagged):     {len(results['FP'])}  <-- safety violation if > 0")
print(f"  False Negative (TRANSFER + untagged): {len(results['FN'])}  <-- coverage gap")
print(f"  True Negative (KEEP + untagged):     {len(results['TN'])}")
print(f"  Proto not in heap:                  {len(results['PROTO_NOT_FOUND'])}")
print(f"  GetAllTags returned null:           {len(results['TAGS_NULL'])}")

if results["FP"]:
    print()
    print("=== FALSE POSITIVES (untouchables tagged - DANGER) ===")
    for r in results["FP"][:50]:
        uid_hex, sp, cp, iv, decision, is_h, is_l, is_s, is_b, alignment, tags = r
        why = []
        if is_h: why.append("hundo")
        if is_l: why.append("lucky")
        if is_s: why.append("shiny")
        if is_b: why.append("best_buddy")
        if alignment != 0: why.append(f"align={alignment}")
        print(f"  {uid_hex} {sp:18s} CP{cp:>4} IV{iv:>5}% kept_because={why} tags={tags}")

# Save full
with open("verify_all_result.json","w") as f:
    json.dump({k: v if k in ("PROTO_NOT_FOUND","TAGS_NULL") else len(v) for k, v in results.items()}, f, indent=2)
    # also dump the actual records
import pickle
with open("verify_all_raw.pkl","wb") as f: pickle.dump(results, f)

sess.detach()
```

```py
"""Verify candidate offsets and find more."""
import json, struct, sqlite3
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import math

data = json.load(open('pokemon_v3.json'))
db = sqlite3.connect('pokemon.db')
c = db.cursor()

c.execute('SELECT uid_hex, pokemon_id, species_name, is_traded, is_lucky, is_hatched_from_egg, is_best_buddy, '
          'level, alignment, alignment_name, costume, original_owner, special_bg_id, location_bg_id, cp '
          'FROM pokemon')
known = {row[0]: row for row in c.fetchall()}

paired = []
for p in data:
    raw = p.get('raw_proto', '')
    if len(raw) < 1000: continue
    bs = bytes.fromhex(raw)
    uid_int = struct.unpack_from('<Q', bs, 32)[0]
    uid_hex = f'{uid_int:016x}'
    if uid_hex not in known: continue
    paired.append((bs, known[uid_hex]))

# Check offset 268 (number ~404-411)
# The gen 9 pokemon might have these as form codes
# But more likely: could be related to "egg incubator type" or "trade timestamp partial"
# Actually 404-411 - looks like a small int. Let me check if it correlates with traded (it's 119 nz)
# and is the trade date span: 404-411 could be decimal-encoded MM-DD-YY?
# More likely: friendship/affinity points

# Look at offset 252 high-bit aligned: 121 nz, distinct=122. If it's an int64 it'd hash a string.
# Let me verify it's an int64 pointing somewhere meaningful.
print('=== Offset 252 inspection ===')
# Check if it correlates with traded (yes - 121 vs 120)
nz252 = set(k[0] for bs, k in paired if struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 252)[0] != 0)
nz252_64 = set(k[0] for bs, k in paired if struct.unpack_from('<q', bs, 252)[0] != 0)
traded = set(k[0] for bs, k in paired if k[3])

print(f'  i32 @252 nz: {len(nz252)}')
print(f'  i64 @252 nz: {len(nz252_64)}')
print(f'  Traded: {len(traded)}')
print(f'  i32 nz - traded: {len(nz252 - traded)}')
print(f'  traded - i32 nz: {len(traded - nz252)}')

# View as int64 - looks like hashed values
print('  Sample int64 @252 (treated as signed):')
for bs, k in paired[:5]:
    if k[3]:  # traded
        v = struct.unpack_from('<q', bs, 252)[0]
        print(f'    {k[2]} (traded from {k[11]}): {v}')

# Offset 252-260 might be 'originalLocation' tied with traded
# It's ALREADY at offset 248 according to current parser (originalLocation = i64(248))
# So 252 is the upper 4 bytes of the 248-byte int64
# Actually offset 248 is already mapped!
# The parse was: originalLocation = i64(248). With i32 view at 252 we see the high half.
# That makes 252 NOT a separate field, it's part of 248.

# But wait - 248 has 92 nz (special_bg related), and 252 has 121 nz. So 248-252 might be 8-byte
# but it has 121 distinct nz patterns. Let me check.

# Actually the build_final says originalLocation = i64(248). Look at it:
v248_64 = Counter()
for bs, k in paired:
    if 248 + 8 > len(bs): continue
    v = struct.unpack_from('<q', bs, 248)[0]
    if v != 0:
        v248_64[v] += 1
print(f'\n  i64 @248: {len(v248_64)} distinct values')

# Top samples
print(f'  samples: {list(v248_64)[:5]}')

# Now look at 268 numbers (407, 404, etc)
print('\n=== Offset 268 - 119 nz, values 404-411 ===')
v268 = Counter()
for bs, k in paired:
    v = struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 268)[0]
    if v != 0:
        v268[v] += 1
print(f'  All values: {sorted(v268.items())}')

# These could be trade levels? Or maybe dates? 407=April 7?
# Let me see what range of pokemon have them
print('  Species with each value:')
for val in sorted(v268):
    cnt = v268[val]
    species = []
    for bs, k in paired:
        if struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 268)[0] == val:
            species.append(k[2])
            if len(species) >= 3: break
    print(f'    {val}: {cnt} - {species}')

# Check: maybe 268 is the high half of int64 264 (tradedTimeMs)?
# tradedTimeMs is at 264. As int64: 264. Let me check.
print('\n  i64 @264 (tradedTimeMs):')
v264_64 = Counter()
for bs, k in paired:
    if 264 + 8 > len(bs): continue
    v = struct.unpack_from('<q', bs, 264)[0]
    if v != 0:
        v264_64[v] += 1
print(f'  Distinct: {len(v264_64)}')
print(f'  Samples: {sorted(v264_64.keys())[:3]}')
# A timestamp 1735191487993 -> 268 high 32 bits = 1735191487993 >> 32 = 404
print(f'  Test: 1735191487993 / 4294967296 = {1735191487993 / 4294967296:.2f}')
# So 268 is the upper half of tradedTimeMs - already mapped via i64(264)

# === MORE OFFSET ANALYSIS ===
# At offset 192 (558 nz) and 196 (121 nz)
print('\n=== Offset 192 (558 nz) ===')
v192_i = Counter()
v192_f = Counter()
for bs, k in paired:
    vi = struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 192)[0]
    vf = struct.unpack_from('<f', bs, 192)[0]
    if vi != 0:
        v192_i[vi] += 1
        if not math.isnan(vf) and not math.isinf(vf):
            v192_f[round(vf, 4)] += 1
print(f'  As i32 top: {v192_i.most_common(10)}')
print(f'  As float top: {v192_f.most_common(10)}')

# 558 is close to ~600 (best buddy? 609 best buddies) - maybe it's a buddy distance counter
nz192 = set(k[0] for bs, k in paired if struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 192)[0] != 0)

print(f'  192 nz - best_buddy: {len(nz192 - bb_set)}')

# Float distribution: let's look closely
print('\n=== Offset 192 float distribution ===')
floats = []
for bs, k in paired:
    v = struct.unpack_from('<f', bs, 192)[0]
    if not math.isnan(v) and not math.isinf(v) and v != 0:
        floats.append(v)
print(f'  Count: {len(floats)}, min={min(floats):.4f}, max={max(floats):.4f}, mean={sum(floats)/len(floats):.4f}')
# Histogram-like
buckets = [0]*10
for v in floats:
    if 0 < v < 1: buckets[0] += 1
    elif v < 10: buckets[1] += 1
    elif v < 50: buckets[2] += 1
    elif v < 100: buckets[3] += 1
    elif v < 500: buckets[4] += 1
    elif v < 1000: buckets[5] += 1
    elif v < 5000: buckets[6] += 1
    else: buckets[7] += 1
print(f'  Buckets [<1, <10, <50, <100, <500, <1000, <5000, >=]: {buckets}')

# Let me also check offset 196 (121 nz, very close to traded count)
print('\n=== Offset 196 (121 nz) - close to traded 120 ===')
v196 = Counter()
for bs, k in paired:
    v = struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 196)[0]

# Hmm, 196 is 1 offset from 192, not 4-byte aligned... could be int8 or int16

# Let me check 192 more carefully - maybe it's "buddy candy awarded" int
# or buddy_total_km (lifetime distance) vs 200 = buddy_distance_walked (per buddy)
# In PoGo: buddy_total_km_walked = total per pokemon, lifetime

# Look at 192 as raw bytes
print('\n=== Offset 192 raw bytes for nz examples ===')
shown = 0
for bs, k in paired:
    v = struct.unpack_from('<i', bs, 192)[0]
    if v != 0 and v < 100:
        print(f'  PID {k[1]} {k[2]}: 192={v} 196={struct.unpack_from("<i", bs, 196)[0]}, raw[192:200]={bs[192:200].hex()}')
        shown += 1
        if shown >= 10: break

# Let me also look at "buddy_pokemon_id" / "current_buddy" candidate
# Probably a bool/byte - check single byte offsets
print('\n=== Single byte distribution between 280-510 ===')
byte_counts = Counter()
for off in range(280, 512):
    cnt_1 = sum(1 for bs, _ in paired if bs[off] == 1)
    cnt_2 = sum(1 for bs, _ in paired if bs[off] == 2)

    if cnt_1 > 5 or cnt_2 > 5:
        print(f'  byte +{off}: =1: {cnt_1}, =2: {cnt_2}')
```

```py
import sqlite3, os

DB = r"C:/Users/Blanco/Desktop/Claude Operations/Phone Maintenance/pogo_extract/pokemon.db"
TAGDIR = r"C:/Users/Blanco/Desktop/Claude Operations/Phone Maintenance/pogo_extract/system/analysis/tagsets"

def load_file(name):
    p = os.path.join(TAGDIR, name)
    s = set()
    with open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            t = line.strip()
            if t:
                s.add(t)
    return s

con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
cur = con.cursor()

# Sanity: distinct in_bag values, iv_total range, NULL checks
print("=== in_bag distinct ===")
for r in cur.execute("SELECT in_bag, COUNT(*) FROM pokemon GROUP BY in_bag ORDER BY in_bag"):
    print(r)
print("=== iv_total distinct (top by value) ===")

for (uh,) in cur.execute("SELECT uid_hex FROM pokemon"):
```
